A bootstrap based on independently computed collinear data, branch-cut constraints and empirical final-entry relations determines both the symbol and the full function. The remaining function-level ambiguity is proportional to $\zeta_2$ times the two-loop planar remainder and is fixed by a single final-entry relation. The weight-three left coproduct factors of the planar and subleading-color results span the same space modulo products; at weight four, the subleading-color result contains four additional nonclassical directions. Through the established maximal-transcendentality correspondence, this compact representation also describes the weight-six subleading-color sector of Higgs-plus-three-gluon amplitudes in QCD. We also construct a four-loop candidate symbol space under a conjectural extension of the three-loop constraints.
papers.authors: Song He

papers.title: From spectroscopy to quantum dynamics: assessing reduced models of a NaCs molecular gate
papers.abstract: We investigate how spectroscopic calibration and basis selection affect predictions for a dipolar-exchange gate between two optically trapped $^{23}$Na$^{133}$Cs molecules. We construct a 128-state molecular Hamiltonian restricted to the $N=0,1$ rotational manifold, fit two effective optical parameters to three bright microwave transitions, and compare the resulting spectrum with four additional lines. In the coherent pair model, changing the optical polarization angle by $+0.1^\circ$ reduces the calculated gate fidelity from 94.64\% to 1.09\% at fixed carrier frequencies. Retuning the carriers and restoring the target Rabi frequencies recovers 89.31\%. The remaining sensitivity reflects changes in the multilevel pair dynamics that are not removed by target-frequency and target-Rabi recalibration. Enlarging the molecular basis produces nonmonotonic changes in fidelity, although the 11-state and 25-state calculations give closely agreeing logical maps after phase alignment. Two controls with isolated transfer probabilities near 98.45\% yield complete-gate fidelities differing by more than 11 percentage points. We relate these comparisons to a sufficient bound on the error of a projected propagator. The numerical tests quantify agreement among selected bases for a specified coherent Hamiltonian.
papers.authors: Marko Gacesa

papers.title: Type IIB Forms and Scalars from an $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ Topological Field Theory with Boundary
papers.abstract: We formulate the scalar and form-field sector of type IIB supergravity as an eleven-dimensional topological field theory with boundary. Unlike the pseudo-action, it is a genuine action principle with manifest global $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ symmetry. The IIB fields arise as edge modes: a boundary term breaks the $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ gauge symmetry to $\mathrm{SO}(2)$, so the axion-dilaton parametrizes $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SO}(2)$, and the boundary field equations give the duality relations, including $F_5$ self-duality. As the action never refers to the axion-dilaton directly, S-duality monodromies become holonomies of a flat connection.
papers.authors: Euihun Joung, J. A. Rosabal

papers.title: Kinetic Cluster Embedding for Qubit Decoherence in Dissipative Spin Baths
papers.abstract: Interpreting the decoherence of a spin qubit requires knowing how the surrounding bath spins behave: whether they fluctuate independently, exchange polarization incoherently, or evolve as coherent groups. These processes can yield the same Hahn-echo coherence time yet produce different coherence signals under pulse control of the qubit. Existing theoretical approaches either capture bath correlations at a cost that grows combinatorially with spin-bath cluster size or neglect polarization transport altogether. We introduce kinetic cluster embedding (KCE), which uses a single dimensionless parameter, comparing the flip-flop coupling of a spin pair with its detuning and linewidth, to decide how each pair must be treated. Pairs that can complete an appreciable exchange oscillation are propagated with the full dissipative quantum dynamics. All other spins are treated as random-telegraph fluctuators coupled through a kinetic network of polarization-transfer rates. We show that for nitrogen-vacancy centers coupled to surface electron spins, KCE propagates about 7 four-spin clusters, compared to more than 10$^5$ propagated by fourth-order master-equation cluster-correlation (ME-CCE4); nevertheless it reproduces ME-CCE4 coherence times to within 15$\%$ for dipolar couplings of order $10^{2}$ times the bath relaxation rate. For a three-dimensional P1 bath, the agreement is within 16$\%$. Coherent multispin clusters emerge as the leading correction to independent fluctuators, and they leave a distinct signature in the CPMG response. Importantly, we find that whether a rate description suffices is set not by coupling strength alone but by whether a pair can exchange polarization coherently before detuning and damping suppress it.
papers.authors: Xiaofei Yu, Jonah Nagura, Stella Wang, Evan J. Villafranca, Peter C. Maurer, Giulia Galli

papers.title: Neutral-atom quantum features as complementary structural encodings for graph learning
papers.abstract: Structural descriptors provide graph neural networks (GNNs) with positional and topological inductive biases. However, widely used classical encodings based on random walks or Laplacian spectra emphasize specific structural statistics of a graph, leaving room for alternative descriptors. Neutral-atom quantum processing units (QPUs) can realize graph-dependent Rydberg Hamiltonians, allowing graph topology to be probed through dynamical correlation measurements. In this work, we use these measurements as quantum graph features (QGFs), providing a complementary, hardware-derived family of structural encoding that is not accurately described by classical features derived from Laplacian and adjacency matrices, even when supplemented with an extended set of random-walk, geometric descriptors and classical physical models. By appropriately selecting the quench parameters of the Hamiltonian, we access two characteristic correlation regimes with distinct structural signatures: antiferromagnetic-like and ferromagnetic-like. On an intrinsic information benchmark of 15 topological and spectral probing tasks, quantum and hybrid quantum-classical features match or surpass classical descriptors on local topological properties. When supplied to message-passing, attention, and graph-transformer backbones, hybrid quantum-classical features yield improvements that are within cross-fold noise on most cells but sign-consistent across architectures. When comparing noiseless, shot-sampled emulation-derived quantum features with a neutral-atom QPU implementation, the downstream hybrid results with compressed hardware features match their emulated counterparts within $0.01$ F$_1$ on all backbones. On a synthetic family of ladder graphs, QGFs distinguish two specific classes, outperforming the strongest classical structural descriptors by a margin exceeding cross-fold variability.
papers.authors: Mathieu Garrigues, Igor O. Sokolov, Matthias Hecker, Lorenzo Moro, Shaheen Acheche

papers.title: Constructing Casimirs for the quantum reflection equation
papers.abstract: We explore the quantum reflection equation in the case of a full-dimensional $n\times n$ matrix $\mathbb A$. Using the technique of $q$-determinants, we find closed expressions for the quantum Pfaffian (in the case of even $n$) and for new quantum Casimirs that are ratios of special quantum (Sklyanin) minors of $\mathbb A$. Special attention is paid to the self-adjointness property of the newly constructed Casimirs. We put forward a conjecture that, adopting a natural ansatz for a quantum deformation of a Casimir of a classical algebra, self-adjointness implies commutativity. We also explore the relationship to networks of quantum cluster variables.
papers.authors: Erik Brodsky, Leonid O Chekhov, Quanyu Tang

papers.title: Talanov dynamics and chirp-controlled rogue-wave formation for the vector nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation
papers.abstract: We study the focusing vector nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation, or Manakov system, for a pair of coupled initial conditions with compactly supported, concave parabolic density profiles and phases depending quadratically on the spatial coordinate. We focus on the natural class of self-similar solutions generated by such profiles, whose dispersionless evolution we refer to as Talanov dynamics. We extend the criterion for blow-up in finite time, first established for a single field, to the Manakov case. For arbitrary initial chirps in the two fields, we provide closed-form expressions for their evolution, and an explicit expression for the time of the gradient catastrophe, if it occurs, and we classify the effect of the coupling on the catastrophe. Depending on the initial chirps, the two fields may catastrophise, or relax, as each would if decoupled. However, coupling can also force the catastrophe in fields that would otherwise relax if decoupled. For identical initial supports, and in the presence of dispersion, we numerically show that the same dispersionless criterion determines, in the semiclassical regime, whether the fully dispersive solution relaxes or develops a rogue wave in each field, whose onset time is accurately predicted by the corresponding dispersionless catastrophe time, in direct analogy with the scalar case. As chirp and amplitude are relatively easy to control experimentally, we expect these results to be relevant to experiments in nonlinear optics and Bose-Einstein condensates, extending to coupled systems observations made for the scalar equation.
papers.authors: G. Ortenzi, G. Roberti, M. Sommacal

papers.title: Features of Non-Local Quantum Correlations in Nuclei
papers.abstract: Classical simulation of quantum many-body systems is challenged by the combined effects of entanglement and non-stabilizerness (magic). Non-local magic, $M^{\mathrm{NL}}_\alpha$, quantifies the component of non-stabilizerness that cannot be removed by local unitary transformations and provides a measure of quantum complexity beyond entanglement alone. It is bounded from below by the antiflatness of the entanglement spectrum, ${F}_A$. We calculate stabilizer R\'enyi entropies, non-local magic, entanglement-spectrum antiflatness, and entanglement entropy in shell-model ground states of more than 260 even-even, odd-even, and odd-odd nuclei, using a bipartition into proton and neutron sectors. We find that the previously established bound $4{F}_A\leq{M}^{\mathrm{NL}}_{\mathrm{lin}}$ holds for every nucleus studied and approaches saturation in the limit of separable states. Odd-odd nuclei exhibit markedly different patterns of entanglement and magic compared with even-even and odd-even systems, revealing distinctive signatures of proton-neutron quantum correlations and providing new insight into the complexity generated by nuclear interactions.
papers.authors: James W. T. Keeble, Caroline E. P. Robin, Federico Rocco, Martin J. Savage

papers.title: Random encoders and expurgation improve 1,873 entries of the Grassl qubit code tables
papers.abstract: I report 192 explicit binary stabilizer codes $[[n,k,d]]$ with $53\le n\le 254$ and $5\le d\le 13$ whose minimum distance exceeds the lower bound listed in Grassl's code tables at the same $(n,k)$: 161 codes by one and 31 by two. Through the standard propagation rules they raise 1,873 entries of the table. For 190 of the codes, a random Clifford encoder is followed by expurgation: every logical operator of weight below the target distance is enumerated, and a few logical operators are promoted to stabilizers so that each low-weight one anticommutes with at least one of them. The other two are obtained by puncturing a code from the table and repairing it in the same way. All 192 distances are exact: the lower bound is certified by exhaustive meet-in-the-middle enumeration of up to $4\times10^{13}$ Pauli operators, and the upper bound by an explicit logical operator of weight $d$. A first-moment count explains the results. Expurgated random codes have about eight more logical qubits than a typical random code of the same length and distance, so they beat the table wherever its best known codes are no better than random. The largest gains, up to nine logical qubits, are at $d\ge9$ and $n\gtrsim170$, where the table often gives a lower bound without an explicit code. The same count predicts improvements at 619 further pairs $(n,d)$. The search was run by AI agents. The codes, their certificates and an independent checker are public.
papers.authors: Marin Girard

papers.title: Neutrino pair annihilation in curved spacetime: a fast moment method and the geometry of flavour conversion
papers.abstract: Neutrino-antineutrino annihilation above black-hole accretion discs is shaped both by general-relativistic transport and by neutrino flavour conversion. Whether these effects can be treated independently depends on how gravity weights the different flavour populations. We investigate this interplay using backward ray tracing in Schwarzschild and Kerr spacetimes, combined with an exact angular-moment formulation of the annihilation kernel that we validate against the analytic spherical solution and published disc calculations. We first establish that flavour-conversion corrections are independent of the spacetime geometry when conversion is uniform and the initial heavy-lepton neutrino emission is negligible. For uniform conversion, this separability remains approximately valid when the flavour-dependent emitting regions overlap: compared with the same discs in flat space, moving with the same local velocities, gravity enhances the deposited energy by factors of 1.4-5, while changing the relative conversion effect by no more than 6% for most temperature profiles considered; conversion that varies across the disc raises this to 22% around a rapidly spinning hole. A qualitatively different regime emerges when heavy-lepton neutrinos originate from an inner ring separated from the electron-flavour emitting regions. Relativistic bending and energy shifts preferentially enhance annihilations involving inner-ring neutrinos, producing relativistic conversion factors up to 2.4 times the flat-space ones. In one configuration, flavour equipartition reduces the deposition by 54% in flat space but increases it by 11% in Kerr spacetime. These results identify the spatial arrangement of flavour-dependent neutrinospheres as a key determinant, in the models considered, of whether flavour conversion and relativistic transport can be treated separately.
papers.authors: Rafael C. R. de Lima, Luciano de Oliveira Junior, Pedro Martins Bailer

papers.title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Annealing for Protein Side-Chain Optimization: A Feasibility Study
papers.abstract: Hybrid quantum-classical annealing solvers are moving from research laboratories toward industrial use, but their advantage over classical optimization appears to be confined to a narrow class of problems. A recent systematic benchmark of the D-Wave hybrid solver against industry-leading classical solvers, across several classes of optimization problems, found it to be most competitive on binary quadratic programs, while noting that few industrial problems take this form. Therefore, identifying real-world industrial problems that can be modeled with this structure is a key challenge. We propose protein side-chain optimization, a core step of computational protein design, as one of these problems: it is natively a binary quadratic program, and its application context requires pools of low-energy solutions, which annealers naturally return. In this feasibility study, we test whether the competitiveness of the hybrid solver against industry-leading classical solvers extends to this problem. On 40 instances derived from 20 experimentally determined protein structures with up to about 200 amino acids and 2000 binary variables, we compare the results achieved with a hybrid solver, run for 5 seconds, against those of the commercial solver Gurobi, run for 10 seconds, 1000 seconds, and 4 hours. The hybrid solver reaches the certified optimum whenever one is available, matches Gurobi's performance on smaller instances, and outperforms it on larger instances, finding lower-energy solutions. These results show that the competitiveness of the hybrid solver on binary quadratic programs, so far observed only on a synthetic benchmark, extends to a real-world problem. This motivates comparisons with classical heuristics specific to protein side-chain optimization.
papers.authors: Valeria B. C. Visani, Simone Reale, Alfonso Gautieri, Elisabetta Di Nitto

papers.title: A Complete Calculus for Hamiltonian Quantum Programming
papers.abstract: Given the forces acting on a quantum particle, a Hamiltonian models its continuous evolution. Quantum computers evolve Hamiltonians to simulate physical systems, to solve optimisation problems, and to estimate eigenvalues, and even the popular circuit abstraction is compiled to Hamiltonians on the hardware. We introduce Hamilton, a process calculus whose parallel operator is the sum of interactions acting simultaneously. Its operational semantics is the Lie-Trotter product formula, which recovers a sum as the limit of ever finer sequential interleavings; compiling a program means halving it to a chosen precision and unrolling the interleaving into a circuit. The semantics is fully abstract, the expressible Hamiltonians are exactly those whose Pauli coefficients have the form $m/2^k$, the precision that successive halving reaches, and the equational theory is complete and decidable. A full implementation compiles Hamilton programs to circuits and decides their equivalence, and Agda proofs sanity-check the core metatheory.
papers.authors: Jacques Carette, Chris Heunen, Robin Kaarsgaard, Neil J. Ross, Amr Sabry

papers.title: Standard Subspaces and Modular Theory -- General Theory and Applications to QFT
papers.abstract: This is a preview of an upcoming monograph on standard subspaces and modular theory. At the moment, it consists of the first chapter. This starts with a gentle introduction to the subject, and then describes the modular theory of standard subspaces, the characterization of their modular data by the KMS condition and reflection positivity, and various constructions of standard subspaces. Further topics in Chapter 1 include the connection of standard subspaces to complexifications and symplectic structures, including their polarizers, and operations with standard subspaces, namely direct sums, direct integrals, and tensor products. Many examples and classification results are included as well. This first chapter also contains a description of the free U(1)-current and some other applications to quantum field theory, such as KMS states of type I factors, the local subspaces of the free Klein--Gordon field, and the entropy operator defined by a standard subspace.
papers.authors: Ricardo Correa da Silva, Gandalf Lechner, Roberto Longo

papers.title: Liouville transforms for ordinary differential equations with distributional coefficients
papers.abstract: We study Liouville transforms for the differential equation $Ju'+qu=wf$ on the real interval $(a,b)$ where $J$ is a constant, invertible, skew-hermitian matrix and $q$ and $w$ are matrices whose entries are distributions of order $0$ with $q$ Hermitian and $w$ non-negative. In particular, we examine their use in the treatment of quasi-regular endpoints and their impact on the Weyl-Titchmarsh $\mathbb M$-function associated with the differential equation.
papers.authors: Rudi Weikard

papers.title: Sign-hedged Beam QAOA:Scaling Quantum Optimization Algorithms
papers.abstract: Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) encodes a combinatorial objective as an Ising Hamiltonian and alternates cost and mixer operations for p rounds. Recursive QAOA (RQAOA) scales further by using the resulting correlations, whether variables tend to agree or disagree, to eliminate variables one at a time. But each inferred sign is accepted irrevocably, so a single early mistake propagates through every later reduction and can discard the global optimum. As elimination proceeds, residuals shrink while effective edge density typically rises, so later decisions face denser Ising problems, a regime that fully connected Sherrington Kirkpatrick (SK) instances stress test directly. This paper proposes sign-hedged beam RQAOA, which retains the variable or pair selected by standard RQAOA, explores both possible sign assignments, keeps the best B residual problems according to a classical score, and completes each survivor with ordinary RQAOA. On frustrated SK instances, where standard recursion collapses to AR 0.474, beam recovers near-optimal AR 0.998 at the same p. We evaluate the workflow on 50+ instances from HamLib and QOBLIB, spanning 4 and 5 regular and Erdos Renyi MaxCut graphs, Sherrington Kirkpatrick (SK) spin glasses, and cardinality-constrained portfolio optimization, with up to 60 qubits and hardware runs on ibm kingston and ibm marrakesh. Matched simulator and device cells show consistent beam rankings: simulation and hardware agree that beam recovers near-optimal approximation ratio (AR) where standard recursion fails. These gains come from additional residual-circuit evaluations, classical pruning, and exact solution of a small core, rather than from increasing p, beam is a decision-side optimization atop fixed-p QAOA/RQAOA, not a claim that quantum circuits alone scale with qubit count.
papers.authors: Anupama Ray, Arush Sharma

papers.title: Testing influence of tides on gravitational wave emission with SPH code PHANTOM
papers.abstract: In this article, we demonstrate how a Newtonian SPH (Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics) code PHANTOM can be used to estimate the tidal contribution to gravitational wave (GW) waveforms. Using a binary neutron star (NS+NS) system with typical masses of 1.5 + 1.5 Msun as an example, we show - by comparing our results with waveforms calibrated against full numerical General Relativity (GR) simulations - that the tidal contribution to GWs can be reliably extracted using as few as about 10$^4$ smoothed particles. Naturally, one must account for the difference in neutron star compactness between Newtonian gravity and general relativity. At separations greater than 100 km, the relative tidal contribution falls below the level of numerical noise inherent in SPH; however, at such distances, GW waveforms for point-like sources are sufficient for detection purposes. For a white dwarf-neutron star (WD+NS) binary with typical masses of 0.6 Msun and 1.5 Msun respectively, a much larger number of smoothed particles is required, along with a separation on the order of tens of thousands of kilometers, as tidal mass transfer and the disruption of the white dwarf begin quite rapidly. Nevertheless, these challenges can be overcome, but the approach is not capable of yielding useful results due to the richness of Newtonian effects. In all cases, it is crucial to perform a hydrostatic/hydrodynamic relaxation (HPR) of the initial models; otherwise, the entire GW signal is lost in the numerical noise.
papers.authors: Marat Sh. Potashov, Sergei I. Blinnikov, Aleksandra V. Mishakina

papers.title: How Many Shots Does a Quantum Reservoir Need? Measurement Cost and Its Scaling in Buffered Quantum Reservoir Computing
papers.abstract: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) inherits from classical reservoir computing the property that only a linear readout is trained, but unlike a classical reservoir its state is never directly observable: every feature is an expectation value estimated from a finite number of measurement shots. The shot budget is therefore a first-class hyperparameter with no classical analogue. Its effect on QRC has recently begun to be studied; what remains unsettled is how a required budget should be defined, and whether competing definitions agree. This paper argues that they do not, and that the disagreement is systematic rather than incidental. This paper distinguishes a \emph{precision budget} $N_\varepsilon$, the shots needed to estimate the reservoir features to a fixed relative accuracy, from a \emph{convergence budget} $N_\star$, the shots needed for the trained readout to approach its own noise-free ceiling. Proposition~\ref{prop:confound} shows that $N_\star$ depends on the noise-free error floor by construction, so that a configuration with a worse floor appears cheaper, and that configurations should therefore be compared at a fixed measurement budget rather than by the budget each needs to reach its own ceiling.
papers.authors: Raman Khurana

papers.title: NLO corrections to charged-current correlators near extremality: non-Abelian hydrodynamics meets AdS$_2$
papers.abstract: We analytically compute the longitudinal charged-current correlator in a near-extremal holographic plasma with quark and isospin chemical potentials, $\mu_q$ and $\mu_3$ respectively. To this end, we study fluctuations of gauge fields around a low-temperature AdS$_5$ Reissner-Nordstr\"om black hole charged both under the quark number and the isospin. The result is obtained at next-to-leading order in a hydrodynamic expansion where apart from the temperature and isospin chemical potential, the frequency and momenta are small compared to the quark chemical potential, $\omega,k,T,\mu_3\ll\mu_q$. This approach captures the interplay between the hydrodynamic-like pole and the tower of infrared modes produced by the AdS$_2$ throat controlling the geometry of the black hole near extremality. At zero isospin chemical potential, the resulting quasinormal-mode formula reproduces the collision of the diffusive pole with the infrared spectrum, while the finite isospin chemical potential lifts this collision. The analytic spectrum agrees precisely with the full numerical results. The next-to-leading-order correlator also substantially improves the spectral function beyond the standard hydrodynamic regime $\omega,k,\mu_3\ll T$, extending the agreement with numerics to larger frequencies and momenta.
papers.authors: Matti J\"arvinen, Elias Kiritsis, Francesco Nitti, Andrea Olzi, Edwan Pr\'eau

papers.title: What are local complementations, really?
papers.abstract: A local complementation at a vertex $v$ of a graph $G$ replaces the induced neighborhood of $v$ with its complement. Local complementations are, at face value, peculiar operations. Yet they famously show up when describing the local Clifford equivalence among graph states, and, because of this, have become a fundamental notion in the study of graph states. Following Bouchet, we show here how local complementations on graphs are more naturally thought of in terms of switchings of (matroid) bases of stabilizer states. Bases and switchings reveal structural properties of stabilizer states that are harder to glean from the graph-theoretic description alone, such as vertex-minors and statistics of local Pauli measurements. Bases also simplify prior proofs about graphs up to local complementations, of which we give several examples. Bases are foundational in the study of (multi)matroids; as such this paper serves as a gentle introduction to the applications of multimatroids to quantum information theory.
papers.authors: Kenneth Goodenough

papers.title: Quantum-enabled measurement of gravitational forces at the milligram scale
papers.abstract: Gravity is by far the weakest among all known interactions. While it dominates the large-scale structure of the universe, gravitational interactions between small masses in the microscopic range remain underexplored because they are too weak to be experimentally accessible. The interface between gravity, described by general relativity, and quantum mechanics, which describes the microscopic world, is of particular interest. From a theory standpoint, these two major descriptions of nature have not been combined in a satisfactory manner. Technology is gradually becoming mature enough such that probing gravity at the microscopic scale, where quantum mechanics and gravity potentially meet, is becoming accessible. Explorations towards genuine quantum gravity have to be carried out under conditions where the gravitating masses possess non-classical properties, which necessitates ultimate protection against disturbances, such as ultralow temperatures and a small range of motion. Here, we present an experiment at millikelvin temperatures, where the gravity due to a micron-range coherent displacement of an 87 mg source mass imprints on the motion of an oscillating membrane loaded with a 1.3 mg test mass. Vibrations of the membrane are measured in the microwave optomechanical scheme, which is a key setup for investigating non-classical motional states of mechanical oscillators. When considering the combination of total source and test masses, our setup presents two orders of magnitude progress in sensing gravity at the small scale, as well as a 35 dB improvement of gravitational sensitivity at kHz frequencies or above. Our setup offers a plausible approach for studying gravitational interactions between masses prepared in non-classical motional states.
papers.authors: Matthew Herbst, Ewa Rej, Joe Depellette, Richa Cutting, Jinhoon Jeong, Mika A. Sillanp\"a\"a

papers.title: Dressed AdS$_4$ black holes in M-theory from the 3d superconformal index
papers.abstract: The superconformal index of 4d $\mathcal N\,{=}\,4$ SYM has been shown to exhibit a rich phase structure, whose holographic interpretation in AdS$_5$ involves (dual-)dressed black holes, gray galaxies, and graviton gas contributions. Here we extend the analysis to 3d CFTs, focusing on ABJM theory and the $\mathcal N=4$ ADHM theory. We study the microcanonical superconformal index with two independent charges at finite $N$ and obtain exact signed state degeneracies up to large charges. The results exhibit the black hole physics expected to emerge at large-$N$, including isolated black holes and black holes dressed by additional matter.
papers.authors: Evan Deddo, Seppe Geukens, Leopoldo A. Pando Zayas, Christoph F. Uhlemann, Wenjie Zhou

papers.title: The Gibbons--Penrose inequality in Minkowski spacetime
papers.abstract: We prove the Gibbons--Penrose inequality for smooth closed spacelike codimension-two submanifolds of Minkowski spacetime whose past null second fundamental form is non-negative. The proof is motivated by the Alexandrov--Bakelman--Pucci technique.
papers.authors: Jingbo Wan, Yipeng Wang

papers.title: Harnessing dimensional leakage for continuous-variable randomness certification
papers.abstract: Semi-device-independent quantum protocols often rely on strict Hilbert-space dimension assumptions that are difficult to satisfy in realistic implementations, particularly with infinite-dimensional optical fields. The almost-qudit framework addresses this issue by quantifying the leakage of quantum states beyond a target subspace. Although such leakage can severely compromise randomness certification for fixed preparation and measurement inputs, we show that averaging over the full input ensemble can mitigate this vulnerability and extend the range of tolerable leakage. This enhanced robustness enables nonzero randomness certification using low-squeezing single-mode Gaussian states and homodyne detection, thus offering an experimentally accessible continuous-variable implementation.
papers.authors: Mois\'es Alves, Tailan S. Sarubi, Vitor L. Sena, Alexandre B. Tacla, Rafael Chaves

papers.title: Effects of Self-Interactions on the Bifurcations in Boson Stars
papers.abstract: Radially excited mini-boson stars have zero modes under static axisymmetric perturbations, at which they bifurcate into axisymmetric configurations with chain-like and ring-like matter distributions. We study how self-interactions affect the $\ell=2$ zero modes of spherical boson stars with one radial node, and construct the chains and rings that bifurcate from them. We consider massive and solitonic boson stars, which have a repulsive quartic self-interaction and a Q-ball type potential, respectively. For massive boson stars, the zero mode persists for all values of the quartic coupling we considered. As the coupling grows, it moves onto the candidate stable branch, so that this branch cannot be entirely stable against $\ell=2$ perturbations, even though sufficiently strong self-interactions are known to quench the radial instability of these stars. For solitonic boson stars, the bifurcations depend strongly on the gravitational coupling. As it decreases, a single family of spherical stars can have multiple zero modes, at which chains and rings alternate, and below a critical coupling the zero modes disappear. In flat spacetime, the rings still exist as static ring-like Q-balls, whereas no chains are found, which suggests that chains need gravity to exist.
papers.authors: Chen Liang

papers.title: A Song of Spice and Ice: A diagonal dual to dS$_3$ & its Galilean flat space limit
papers.abstract: We propose a diagonal CFT dual to asymptotically de Sitter spacetimes in three dimensions (3d), constructed from the holomorphic part of the CFT dual at the future boundary and the antiholomorphic part of the CFT dual at the past boundary, in part inspired by an antipodal map between the two CFT copies. This gives equal and opposite imaginary central charges for the holomorphic and antiholomorphic sectors. The corresponding diagonal holographic energy-momentum tensor expectation values are constructed from the Wavefunction at the future boundary and its conjugate. This enables a recovery of the entropy of $dS_3$, as well as a family of complex Kerr $dS_3$ spacetimes with two real horizons, by a Cardy formula. We then explore the flatspace limit of our dS construction. With the central charges as above, the flatspace limit naturally induces a Galilean contraction on the dual diagonal 2d CFT, in contrast to the more familiar Carrollian limit when 3d Asymptotically Flat Spacetime (AFS) is approached from $AdS_3$. The corresponding limit for the complex Kerr family above leaves the inner horizon intact, resulting in flat space complex black holes ($\mathbb{C}$BH) that are closely related to flat space cosmologies which arise from BTZ black holes in AdS$_3$. We recover the entropy of these $\mathbb{C}$BHs by the BMS-Cardy formula.
papers.authors: Arjun Bagchi, Sharang Rajesh Iyer, K. Narayan

papers.title: Reflecting Baths and Black Hole Interior Islands in JT Gravity
papers.abstract: We study the evolution of entanglement entropy within the island prescription in Jackiw-Teitelboim gravity coupled to finite non-gravitating baths bounded by reflecting walls. For free massless Dirac matter, we study the evolution of entanglement entropy, explicitly accounting for correlations induced by the reflecting boundaries. For sufficiently short baths, the no-island entropy saturates below the thermodynamic black hole entropy, avoiding the usual information paradox associated with its unbounded growth. For larger baths, reflected correlations drive the exterior quantum extremal surface toward the future horizon, leading to a temporary disappearance of the the near-horizon exterior island branch. We find that this branch first appears at a scrambling-like scale, and it reappears at a time that is proportional to the size of the bath. We extend the extremization across the horizon using regular Kruskal coordinates and identify real quantum extremal surfaces in the black hole interior. We show that, in the parameter regime studied, interior island configurations provide the dominant contribution to the radiation entropy during the exterior disappearance time interval, resolving the reappearance of the information paradox in an exterior-only description.
papers.authors: Dmitry S. Ageev, Anastasia N. Zueva

papers.title: Phentax: A JAX implementation of the IMRPhenomTHM waveform model
papers.abstract: The upcoming Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) is expected to be sensitive to thousands of white dwarf (WD) binaries in our galaxy, extreme mass ratio inspirals (EMRIs) of stellar-mass compact objects into massive black holes, stellar-mass black hole binaries (SOBHBs) in their early inspiral phase, and, crucially, massive black hole binaries (MBHBs) with masses in the range of $10^4$-$10^7 M_\odot$. The presence of such a large number of signals requires joint inference of all parameters across all sources present in the data, an approach referred to as "global fit". This requires evaluating hundreds of thousands of waveform templates, which can be computationally expensive. To address this challenge, we present $\texttt{Phentax}$, a $\texttt{JAX}$ re-implementation of the $\texttt{IMRPhenomTHM}$ waveform model. This is a state-of-the-art time-domain phenomenological waveform model for comparable-mass binary black holes that includes the effects of higher-order modes. Given this, $\texttt{IMRPhenomTHM}$ is one of the models currently used to simulate and analyze MBHB signals in LISA. With $\texttt{Phentax}$, we provide a fast, easy-to-batch, and differentiable implementation of this waveform model to accelerate the development of LISA global fit algorithms.
papers.authors: Alessandro Santini, Diganta Bandopadhyay, Jonathan Gair

papers.title: Entanglement in Collective Neutrino Oscillations on a Quantum Computer
papers.abstract: Simulations on a quantum computer have been propounded as a next-generation tool for studying neutrino flavour oscillations in dense environments like supernovae or neutron star mergers. However, quantum advantage hinges on the presence of quantum entanglement in the neutrino ensemble, and it has been argued that such entanglement becomes negligible in the limit of large neutrino number density. Here, we address this question by explicitly simulating the multiparticle dynamics of entangled neutrino ensembles with a varying number of particles, $N$, on both classical and quantum hardware, and comparing our results to those obtained with conventional ``mean-field'' methods based on Boltzmann-type kinetic equations. For simple toy systems, we demonstrate both analytically and numerically that, indeed, the predictions of full multiparticle simulations agree with those of mean-field methods in the large-$N$ limit. Along the way, we develop novel algorithms for the efficient simulation of entangled neutrino gases on both classical and quantum hardware. We then discuss physical situations in which an entangled neutrino system \emph{cannot} be described through mean-field dynamics alone and quantum entanglement therefore becomes phenomenologically relevant. We comment on the conditions under which these scenarios may be realized in supernova cores or neutron star mergers.
papers.authors: Katarina Bleau, Nikolina Ilic, Joachim Kopp, Ushak Rahaman, Xin Yue Yu

papers.title: Exploring topological signatures of quantum Fisher information scaling in graph states
papers.abstract: Graph states are a versatile resource for quantum metrology, and their quantum Fisher information (QFI) has a closed-form expression in terms of the underlying graph: it counts pairs of vertices with identical neighborhoods. It remains unclear, however, which global structural properties of a graph determine whether its QFI exceeds the standard quantum limit (SQL). Here we ask whether topological invariants, namely the Betti numbers of the graph's clique complex, capture this behavior, and we address the question numerically with two complementary approaches. First, we randomly add or delete edges in balanced complete multipartite graphs, which combine a QFI beyond the SQL with a single nonvanishing higher Betti number. Edge addition eventually destroys both the metrological advantage and the nontrivial topology. Under edge deletion, by contrast, higher Betti numbers persist well after the QFI has dropped to the SQL. Second, we start from Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi random graphs, whose QFI does not typically exceed the SQL, and maximize a chosen Betti number with a Monte Carlo search. The search drives the graphs toward near-extremal multipartite structures whose QFI lies well beyond the SQL. Our results show that topological optimization offers a route to metrologically useful graph states, but also that Betti numbers alone do not determine the QFI.
papers.authors: Majid Hassani, Patrick Emonts, Jordi Tura

papers.title: Density kernel and temporal quantum information probes in double-scaled SYK
papers.abstract: Entanglement is conventionally defined through a Hilbert space bipartition on a fixed time slice. Recent work has generalized this notion to multiple times through a non-Hermitian density kernel constructed from temporal correlation functions, encoding causal response, temporal non-classicality and quantum dynamics. We construct this kernel in the double-scaled Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev (DSSYK) model using its exact chord Hilbert space formulation and study the resulting temporal information diagnostics. The direct sum structure of chord space naturally introduces a coarse-graining under which coherence between different chord sectors is removed. We show that the corresponding kernel measures quantify how information is dynamically transferred across subregions in the chord Hilbert space. We find that decreasing $\lambda$ enhances the propagation of temporal correlation across chord sectors, as well as the loss of memory within a fixed sector. This accelerated temporal dynamics in the small $\lambda$ limit coincides with the emergence of a semiclassical gravity description. Depending on the chord space partition, the probes exhibit either saturation, a growth followed by a decay, or temporary memory loss. The characteristic propagation time is nicely captured by a wavefront picture in Krylov space, with position-dependent hopping parameters that are determined by the DSSYK Lanczos coefficients. Finally, given the quantum sine-dilaton gravity description of DSSYK and its connections to de Sitter holography, our results provide a controlled setting for probing temporal quantum correlations across quantum and semiclassical gravitational regimes, and motivate a geometric interpretation of the density kernel.
papers.authors: Johanna Erdmenger, Maximilian Gaschler, Jonathan Karl, Arnab Kundu, Georg Setzer

papers.title: Conley index theory for asymptotically autonomous systems and UV-to-IR connections
papers.abstract: Many non-equilibrium systems, such as expanding plasmas, evolve by equations that depend explicitly on time and interpolate between autonomous early-time (UV) and late-time (IR) limits. After time is compactified, fixed points lie on invariant boundary fibers, where the Conley index is one-sided and blind to the UV. For time dependence that admits a $C^1$ compactification, we reflect the extended phase space across these fibers. Both sheets of the double run from the UV to the IR, and the UV index reappears, suspended by one degree. Extending one sheet slightly beyond both fibers gives an explicit UV-to-IR transport map between the Conley indices of the limit systems, and its non-vanishing forces connecting solutions. If one block with a fixed strict entrance/exit decomposition serves every frozen system, this map is an isomorphism at every admissible rate. If the block also has nonzero relative homology, the isolated invariant sets of the two limits are connected at every rate. In the Gubser flow of Israel-Stewart theory, the separatrix between two classes of initial data is a transversal connection at every finite relaxation scale $c$, with splitting $\Delta(c)\propto1/c$. In the Bjorken flow at the lowest moment truncation, we prove existence and uniqueness of the attractor solution without regularization. For the three-dimensional Gubser system we construct the global Morse decomposition. In the one-loop flow of the $(4+\epsilon)$-dimensional $O(N)$ model with cubic anisotropy, a shift of $N$ through $N=4$ has vanishing transport map, but a driven connection and a nonzero connecting homomorphism detect it at every rate.
papers.authors: Alireza Behtash, Syo Kamata, Mauricio M. Martinez

papers.title: Universality in Quantum Many-Body Spin Ratchets
papers.abstract: We consider a class of quantum circuits, known as quantum many-body spin ratchets, which act on alternating spin chains with two distinct spin types on even and odd sites. This setup breaks parity symmetry and exhibits chiral transport. It has been shown that the drift velocity in the case of integrable, SU(2)-symmetric quantum spin ratchets is universal, and conjectured that the same holds in the non-integrable case. Here, we prove that this universal drift is exact at all times, requiring only translation invariance and U(1) symmetry. Furthermore, we prove that it is sufficient for the circuit to be translation-invariant on average by deriving the same result in the random case. Finally, we demonstrate that breaking translation invariance immediately results in deviations from this universal prediction.
papers.authors: Andrea Azzali, Marko Ljubotina

papers.title: AdS to dS Flows Dual to Pseudo-Hermitian Theories
papers.abstract: We construct generalizations of ''centaur" geometries in more than two dimensions as solutions of Einstein gravity coupled to a ghost scalar. The solutions interpolate between asymptotically anti-de Sitter and asymptotically de Sitter spacetimes, with the two asymptotic regions separated by a horizon. A holographic interpretation is that they are dual to pseudo-Hermitian theories obtained from the continuation of real couplings and operators to purely imaginary values. One family of solutions is obtained from a supergravity theory that is a consistent truncation with a known embedding in string theory. We study the thermodynamic and linear stability of the solutions, and determine the uplift of the supergravity solutions to eleven dimensions.
papers.authors: Jos\'e M. Begines, Ant\'on F. Faedo, Carlos Hoyos, Daniele Musso

papers.title: Magic Is in the Eye of the Measure
papers.abstract: Magic, or nonstabilizerness, is the quantum resource behind universal quantum computation. Its applications in high-energy and nuclear physics rely almost exclusively on the stabilizer R\'enyi entropy (SRE), although magic has no unique measure. For two qubits, we compare the SRE with three measures defined through optimizations over stabilizer states: the min- and max-relative entropies of magic and the logarithmic free robustness. We determine the maximal-magic states of all four measures, with exact proofs, and find that they depend on the measure. In the determination of the weak mixing angle from minimal magic in M{\o}ller scattering, the min-relative entropy gives an energy-dependent value that differs from that of the SRE, whereas the max-relative entropy and the logarithmic free robustness give $\sin^2\theta_W=1/4$ at all energies. We trace this difference to the non-analytic structure of the optimization-based measures. Physical conclusions drawn from extremizing magic can thus depend on the measure.
papers.authors: Zhi-Heng Shen, Zhewei Yin, Hao-Lin Zhang

papers.title: Primordial or Post-Inflationary: Distinguishing the Origin of Scale-Dependent Features in the CMB
papers.abstract: Physics beyond the Standard Model, whether of primordial or post-inflationary origin, can leave scale-dependent signals in the anisotropies of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB). In this work, we study how distinguishable these broad classes of signals are and quantify their level of degeneracy. In this initial investigation, for primordial features, we limit ourselves to those of the ``sharp'' and ``resonant'' kinds; for post-inflationary features, we consider two qualitatively distinct models: exotic energy injection, which deposits energy into the primordial plasma and modifies the global thermodynamic history, and early dark energy (EDE), which affects the CMB through the background expansion and gravitational perturbations. By studying representative examples, we find that while primordial features can leave oscillatory signatures in the CMB power spectrum with essentially arbitrary frequency and running, the post-inflationary models considered here produce qualitatively different patterns that cannot generically reproduce the characteristic running of primordial feature oscillations. We verify these findings first with a principal component analysis, and show using only the most significant principal components that there are no significant degeneracies between the primordial and post-inflationary features considered here, and secondly with a full likelihood analysis, which shows that the resulting posteriors do not change significantly when considering individual classes of models or combinations of primordial/post-inflationary features. While the two post-inflationary models probe distinct physical mechanisms and both are implemented in a simplified, phenomenological fashion, the methods used in this work can be generalized to include more realistic signals or other classes of signals.
papers.authors: Matteo Braglia, Wenzer Qin, Xingang Chen, Tracy R. Slatyer

papers.title: Fermionic Kaluza-Klein Reductions
papers.abstract: We work out the Kaluza--Klein (KK) compactification on a general product spacetime for free spin-1/2 and spin-3/2 fields in arbitrary dimension. The analysis is performed at the level of the action, and the resulting lower-dimensional theory describes infinite towers of massive particles whose masses are related to the eigenvalues of the Dirac and Rarita--Schwinger operators on the internal space. A Hodge-like decomposition is used to write down a KK ansatz for spin-3/2 fields, and the fate of gauge invariance is discussed.
papers.authors: Francesco Bertucci

papers.title: Analytic Bounds on Conformal Defect Spectra
papers.abstract: Conformal defects describe impurities and boundaries at criticality. Their stability depends on the scaling dimensions of operators localized on the defects, but these dimensions are often difficult to determine. We derive analytic upper bounds on the lowest nonvacuum scaling dimension using only two defect entropies and the dimension of a defect-changing operator. The bounds identify when relevant operators must appear on the defect with larger defect entropy. They follow from the conformal bootstrap of four-point functions of defect-changing operators and apply to unitary conformal line defects and to conformal boundaries in two-dimensional CFTs. The Ising and Potts models provide exact checks. In three-dimensional $O(N)$ models, we apply the bounds to direct sums of pinning field defects with symmetry-related orientations. Data from a single such defect exclude stable impurity order with three or more orientations in $O(2)$ and $O(3)$, or four or more in $O(4)$, for any geometry of the orientations, and require a relevant domain-wall operator between individually stable pinning field defects at every nonzero relative angle up to $120^\circ$ in $O(3)$ and up to $109.47^\circ$ in $O(4)$. A direct fuzzy-sphere computation of the lowest domain-wall dimension at different relative angles for $N=2,3,4$ is consistent with these bounds and indicates that, within this class of impurities, only two-state order remains a candidate for stable order in $O(3)$ and $O(4)$, while none survives in $O(2)$. A separate application to AdS/BCFT shows that, at fixed unequal brane tensions, a light boundary-condition-changing operator requires additional light primaries on the boundary with larger boundary entropy.
papers.authors: Yuma Furuta, Wataru Harada, Yuya Kusuki, Yin Tang

papers.title: Discreetly Conformal: Higher-Order Chiral Scalars and the Discrete Series
papers.abstract: With its constant shift symmetry gauged, a massless scalar on two-dimensional flat space defines a conformal field theory whose classical phase space is equivalent to that of a chiral and an anti-chiral Floreanini--Jackiw scalar. We show that this picture generalizes: After gauging a larger set of the shift symmetries of the massless scalar field, it decomposes into a pair of generalized chiral and anti-chiral scalars, described by actions with higher-order spatial derivatives. We spell out their physical and gauge symmetries, and show how these give rise to the hidden conformal symmetry of the scalar with gauged shift symmetries. This lifts to de Sitter space, where we find that the discrete series scalars also decompose into these generalized chiral scalars, providing an explanation for their hidden conformal symmetry.
papers.authors: Calvin Y. -R. Chen, Kurt Hinterbichler, Samanta Saha, Thomas Yan

papers.title: Andreev reflections and optimal truncation in the unitary Fermi droplet
papers.abstract: We study the unitary Fermi gas in an external trap in the double-scaling limit of large flavor number N and large charge Q at fixed Q/N. At leading order, the problem reduces to the spectral zeta function of a BdG operator in an inhomogeneous pairing background. The grand potential admits a gradient expansion with distinct bulk and edge sectors. We show that when the trap is harmonic, the bulk sector expansion terminates: beyond the first three terms every bulk contribution integrates to zero. This cancellation is general and follows from zeros of the Euler beta function computed in the Son-Wingate effective field theory, independent of the low-energy constants. The truncation persists for anisotropic traps in any odd dimension. All higher-order dependence for harmonic potentials is therefore carried by the droplet edge. For anharmonic traps, the asymptotic bulk series is factorially divergent. Using a heat-kernel WKB analysis, we show that its large-order growth, sign oscillations, and optimal truncation are fixed by complex periodic orbits of the BdG problem, which are analytic continuations of Andreev reflections. We numerically confirm the predicted Borel singularities for quartic and sextic traps.
papers.authors: Silas R. Beane, Adele Le Borgne, Domenico Orlando, Susanne Reffert, Maximilian Schwick

papers.title: Thermodynamics of Speed and Efficiency with Quantum Feedback
papers.abstract: Rapid thermodynamic operations generally entail irreversible dissipation, giving rise to trade-offs between operating speed and thermodynamic cost. Yet, how quantum feedback fundamentally reshapes these trade-offs remains elusive. Here, we derive a finite-time current--dissipation relation for continuously monitored open quantum dynamics with jump feedback. From this fundamental relation, we establish a quantum speed limit and a power-efficiency trade-off for stationary information engines, identifying how feedback affects state transformations and the performance of engines through both informational entropy and direct dynamical contributions. Our results provide a quantitative foundation for fast, low-dissipation quantum thermodynamics in the presence of feedback control, exemplified by attaining the generalized Landauer bound in finite-time information erasure and approaching unit information efficiency at finite power in the large-system limit of a collective engine.
papers.authors: Yue Liu, Ryotaro Honma, Ruicheng Bao, Tan Van Vu

papers.title: Constraints on Quintom Dark Energy Model with Matter Interaction
papers.abstract: The quintom model consisting of quintessence and phantom scalar fields with linear coupling to matter is explored and constrained by updated DESI and supernovae type Ia~(SNIa) observational data. The matter interaction is assumed only between phantom and matter and the quintessence self potential is in an exponential form. The quintom evolution shows a class of solutions with phantom crossing scenario consistent with the current DESI data. From low redshift observations, we place constraints on the model with BAO data from DESI and distance measurements from SNIa Pantheon+ samples and SH0Es. For high-redshift constraints, we use CMB priors from Planck and found that the quintom model gives the best-fit Hubble parameter $H_{0}=65.780~(68.736)$~km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$ for DESI+CMB+SNIa~(+SH0ES) respectively. The marginalized statistical constrained values are $H_{0}=66.21\pm 0.84~(68.49^{+0.46}_{-0.40})$~km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$ for DESI+CMB+SNIa~(+SH0ES) respectively. Using the BBN prior for high-redshift constraints, the corresponding best-fit values for DESI+BBN+SNIa~(+SH0ES) constraints are $H_{0}=63.999~(71.962)$~km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$ and the marginalized statistical values for DESI+BBN+SNIa~(+SH0ES) constraints are $H_{0}=61.6^{+6.6}_{-3.0}~(71.86\pm 0.88)$~km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$ respectively. Generally, adding SH0ES significantly raises the best-fit and marginalized value of $H_{0}$ for all datasets. In comparison to $\Lambda$CDM, the interacting quintom model gives lower values of $\sigma_{8}=0.74-0.79$ for combination of datasets with CMB prior. Lastly, the fifth-force constraint from local scale solar system Cassini probe is estimated, we find the constraint on the phantom-matter coupling $|\delta|<3.3\times 10^{-3}$.
papers.authors: Chakkrit Kaeonikhom, Theppawan Rukpakawong, Piyabut Burikham

papers.title: Integral zeros of Krawtchouk polynomials and quantum entanglements
papers.abstract: In Heo and Kiem (2019), the authors raised a problem relating integral zeros of binary Krawtchouk polynomials, parametrized by quadruples $(m,n,k,\ell)$ with $m\le n$ and $k\le \ell$, to the existence of pairs of subspaces satisfying the range criterion in quantum information theory, and settled the symmetric case $k=\ell$. In this paper, we solve the problem for the following three asymmetric families: $(m,n,k,\ell)=(3,t^2-1,t(t-1)/2,t(t+1)/2)$, $t\ge2$; $(m,n,k,\ell)=(4,3t^2+2t-1,(3t^2-t)/2,(3t^2+5t+2)/2)$, $t\ge2$; $(m,n,k,\ell)=(4,3s^2+4s,(3s^2+s)/2,(3s^2+7s+4)/2)$, $s\ge1$. The remaining cases are sporadic zeros, with only finitely many for each $m\ge5$.
papers.authors: Jaeseong Heo, Young-Hoon Kiem, Chul-hee Lee

papers.title: On the Volume Conjectures for Dehn-filled $3$-manifolds along fundamental shadow link complements with big volume
papers.abstract: We prove the Volume Conjecture and the Asymptotic Expansion Conjecture for closed oriented hyperbolic $3$-manifolds obtained by integral Dehn-fillings along a fundamental shadow link complement, provided that their volumes are sufficiently close to that of the complement. More generally, we show that the conjectured asymptotic expansions hold for pairs obtained by change-of-pair operations on a fundamental shadow link complement whenever the volume of the corresponding hyperbolic cone manifold is sufficiently close to that of the complement. A key ingredient in the proof is the introduction of extended quantum $6j$-symbols and a Weak Reflection Symmetry satisfied by them. The Weak Reflection Symmetry is established by relating the extended quantum $6j$-symbols to the $b$-$6j$ symbols through a real Gevrey-$1$ estimate and a truncated Borel-Laplace transform.
papers.authors: Yunpeng Meng, Baojun Wu, Tian Yang, Yuxuan Yang

papers.title: pfoqcompiler: Efficient Compilation of Quantum Control in Recursive First-Order Quantum Programs
papers.abstract: Recursive quantum control allows for simple and concise descriptions of algorithms. However, a naive circuit compilation sequentializes the different branches of the quantum if-statement and results in an exponential increase in circuit depth. Existing techniques can parallelize these branches, but do so at the cost of an exponential number of ancillary qubits. We present pfoqcompiler, a compiler targeting Qiskit for the first-order quantum programming language FOQ that exploits program structure to merge compatible recursive procedure calls across quantum branches. We introduce weaker syntactically-checkable conditions for well-foundedness, recursive halving, and uniformity, while preserving previously demonstrated complexity characterizations. For weakly well-founded bounded-width programs, the compiler produces polynomial-size circuits; weakly recursively halving programs additionally yield polylogarithmic depth, while weak uniformity removes the asymptotic overhead of branch sequentialization.
papers.authors: M\'ario Silva (LMF, QuaCS), Alexandre Guernut (MOCQUA), Marco Lewis (LMF, QuaCS)

papers.title: Explicit Symmetry Breaking in Non-Abelian Scalar Theories and One-Loop Renormalization
papers.abstract: Non-Abelian gauge theories coupled to scalar fields are fundamental in particle physics, yet they often face high-energy instabilities. In this work, we start by analyzing the classical $SU(2)$ complex scalar model, mapping the scalar multiplet into a real $SO(2N)$ representation to formalize its generalization to $SU(N)$. Within this classical setup, we introduce an explicit gauge symmetry breaking exclusively in the scalar sector by splitting the mass parameters and quartic self-coupling constants. Moving to the quantum level, we employ the background field method and the Schwinger-DeWitt technique to compute the exact one-loop divergences, explicitly demonstrating the renormalizability of the broken theory. Finally, we derive the Renormalization Group equations and analyze the fixed points of the flow. It is shown that this explicit symmetry breaking asymptotically destabilizes the theory, driving the scalar couplings away from the origin and inevitably leading to a Landau pole.
papers.authors: Lucas Ducastelo de C. C. Lima

papers.title: The K\"ahler Stability Wall in Perturbative Brane--Antibrane Inflation
papers.abstract: Perturbative brane--antibrane inflation requires the physical K\"ahler volume to remain stabilized while the anti-D3 sector supplies the inflationary energy. This paper shows that this requirement imposes an exact analytic boundary on the allowed anti-D3 tension. In the leading nilpotent effective theory, the K\"ahler minimum and the decompactification barrier disappear through a saddle-node degeneration determined by \(U_\sigma=U_{\sigma\sigma}=0\). The positive-tension branch of this boundary is solved in closed form and uniformized by a single real parameter. The same solution fixes the local scaling of the K\"ahler mass, barrier height, and canonical distance to the endpoint. Integrating out the volume modulus reveals a Schur-complement singularity, showing that the adiabatic single-field description fails at the same boundary unless the inflaton--volume mixing is suppressed. The result is then translated into necessary flux-arithmetic filters involving the warped throat, D3 tadpole, conifold control, scalar normalization, and the full K\"ahler-sector mass matrix. Numerical tests verify the critical locus, the saddle-node scaling laws, and the resulting sparse throat-flux filtration. These conditions are necessary for compact realizations; no compact vacuum is asserted without the corresponding global and Wilsonian control checks.
papers.authors: Swapnil Kumar Singh

papers.title: Dualities in one-dimensional quantum lattice models: Lie groups, Schur-Weyl duality and symmetry breaking
papers.abstract: We present a systematic framework for gauging continuous symmetries, and show that the Schur-Weyl duality arises naturally as a realization of this construction with open boundary conditions. Restricting to compact Lie group symmetries, we construct dual models for one-dimensional quantum lattice models exhibiting those symmetries. We demonstrate that matrix product operators enable the explicit construction of intertwiners between the dual theories and their (non-invertible) symmetries. With closed boundary conditions, we can relate the full spectrum of these dual theories by considering all possible twisted boundary conditions. We illustrate how the Peter-Weyl transform appears when the duality acts on the boundary Hilbert space of a $G$-symmetric model. The presented framework generalizes previous work on dualities for unitary fusion category symmetric models. It exemplifies how dualities for both finite and continuous symmetries rely on the relation between a bond algebra and a representation of the symmetry in the lattice as double centralizers. We argue that dual non-invertible spontaneous symmetry breaking is the mechanism that underlies symmetric tensor network algorithms. We illustrate these results for $U(1)$- and $SU(2)$-symmetric quantum lattice models.
papers.authors: Dante Bosgoed, Frank Verstraete, Laurens Lootens

papers.title: Clifford BMW Categories and Conformal Embeddings of Types B C and D
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give diagrammatic descriptions of the quantum subgroups coming from conformal embeddings of the form $\mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{g}, \check{h}) \subset \mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{so}_{\dim \mathfrak{g}}, 1)$ for $\mathfrak{g}\in \left\{\mathfrak{so}_N, \mathfrak{sp}_{2N}\right\}$, as well as the conformal embeddings of the form $\mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{sp}_{2r + 2}, 2r) \subset \mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{so}_{\dim \mathfrak{sp}_{2r + 2}}, 1)$, extending the techniques of Edie-Michell and Snyder which applied to conformal embeddings of the form $\mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{sl}_r, r) \subset \mathcal{V}(\mathfrak{so}_{\dim \mathfrak{sl}_r}, 1)$. Our main conceptual innovation is the use of fermion condensation to construct a continuous family of planar superalgebras, which we call the Clifford BMW supercategories. The tower of endomorphism algebras, $CW_n(\sigma, \epsilon)$ is a combination of Birman Wenzl Murakami algebras and Clifford algebras, much in the spirit of the Hecke Clifford algebras. This tower of algebras appears to be new, and already yields some exciting combinatorics.
papers.authors: August Bergquist

papers.title: A hierarchy of physics-embedded neural operators for structural dynamic surrogate modeling
papers.abstract: Structural-response surrogates must capture moving resonances, phase changes, and unequal-amplitude transfer channels during optimization or health-state changes. Physics-embedded learning seeks FEA-level accuracy at lower cost by embedding physics in inputs, forward passes, losses, and backpropagation. We propose Modal Rational (MR), mapping structural features to modal quantities for analytical frequency-response reconstruction. The Physics-Guided Modal Operator Network (PGMON) adds bounded frequency, damping, and residual-flexibility corrections. Modal Operator with Structural GELU and Anchored-SIREN Correction (MOSAIC) denotes the bounded spectral-discrepancy framework used here; MOSAIC-MR and MOSAIC-PGMON add such discrepancies. They support finite-dimensional maps and physical decoders for future neural operators; evidence is fixed-topology, not a completed operator comparison. Two 20,000-design populations are studied: an 80 m steel truss tower with variable member areas and attached masses, and a tapered shell beam with ten variable station masses. Archived tests cover ten designs and seven acceleration histories per structure; they are benchmarks, not seismic-design assessments. With 5% reference modal damping, MR, PGMON, and MOSAIC give mean displacement-history errors of 0.73-0.76% for the tower and 0.029-0.116% for the beam, against declared band-limited modal references. Supplied modal frequencies are distinguished from design-only use; unequal parameter counts and training settings are explicit. Error analysis separates learned modal discrepancies, truncation, and excitation weighting, explaining acceleration and difficult-tower limits and risks of blind use. Results support physically structured prediction but limit claims about generalization, computational savings, and added corrections. Next is developing and validating neural operators around these architectures.
papers.authors: Amir Nasrollahi, Mehmet Sefa Orak

papers.title: Chromatic Spherical and Renormalized Reshetikhin-Turaev Invariants for Drinfeld Centers
papers.abstract: We give invariants of pairs $(M,\Gamma)$ consisting of a closed connected oriented three-manifold and an oriented framed ribbon graph embedded in $M$ colored by the Drinfeld center of a unimodular finite chromatic category $\mathcal C$. This invariant generalizes the chromatic spherical and renormalized Reshetikhin-Turaev invariants of three-manifolds. We use Heegaard-Graph diagrams which represent the pair $(M,\Gamma)$ and use the data of a unimodular chromatic category and objects of the Drinfeld center to construct the invariant. We define a ribbon graph associated to embedded framed links to obtain an invariant of pairs $(M,L)$. We show that if $L$ is the empty link, then the invariant recovers the chromatic spherical invariant, and if $M$ is the three-sphere, then the invariant recovers the renormalized Reshetikhin-Turaev invariant from the Drinfeld center. The relationship is proven by recovering a chromatic structure for the center induced by that from $\mathcal C$. The main theorem of the paper demonstrates that if the graph is a link $L$ colored by a generator in the Drinfeld center, then we recover the chromatic spherical invariant of the surgery manifold $M(L)$, contributing to a proof of the relationship between the chromatic spherical and renormalized Reshetikhin-Turaev invariants for unimodular chromatic categories, generalizing a recent result for unimodular Hopf algebras by Reina. To this end, we give a Heegaard diagram for $M(L)$ coming from the Heegaard-Link diagram representing the pair $(M,L)$.
papers.authors: Nicolas Bridges, Shawn Cui, Nathan Geer

papers.title: Quasi-equilibrium tidal folds of white dwarfs around rotating black holes in shift-symmetric Einstein--scalar--Gauss--Bonnet gravity
papers.abstract: We examine how the geometry of rotating black holes in linear, shift-symmetric Einstein--scalar--Gauss--Bonnet (EsGB) gravity changes the limiting tidal equilibria of white dwarfs (WDs). The relativistic tidal field is obtained from numerical EsGB backgrounds in a parallel-transported frame and coupled to a compressible affine model. Comparisons with Kerr black holes matched in Arnowitt--Deser--Misner (ADM) mass and angular momentum show a positive shift in the orbital frequency at the tidal fold. At fixed spin the relative correction follows an approximately quadratic dependence on the EsGB coupling, consistent with the leading response of the metric to the scalar field. Over the sampled backgrounds, the relative correction reaches order $10^{-3}$. Black hole rotation also changes the relation between the tidal fold and the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO): the sampled prograde folds remain outside the ISCO, while retrograde folds move inside it at higher spins. Orbital orientation therefore controls whether tidal equilibrium is lost before the orbital stability limit is reached. For the stellar and black hole masses considered here, the characteristic gravitational wave (GW) frequencies fall in the millihertz band relevant to planned space based interferometers. Future GW observations capable of resolving deviations from Kerr predictions could constrain the EsGB coupling.
papers.authors: Shoupan Liu, Meilin Liu, Yu Wang, Yunqi Liu, Bin Wang

papers.title: Circuit Complexity of Scalar and Tensor Perturbations in Luminal Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet Inflation
papers.abstract: We investigate the circuit complexity of primordial scalar and tensor perturbations in the luminal branch of Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet (EGB) inflation. We construct the Hamiltonians from the quadratic actions and derive the evolution equations for the squeezing parameters. Although the tensor propagation speed is fixed to unity, the Gauss-Bonnet (GB) coupling remains dynamical through the scalar and tensor pump fields. We then calculate the Nielsen circuit complexity of the corresponding two-mode squeezed states. The GB correction produces a clear separation between the squeezing amplitudes, while the squeezing angles remain nearly phase locked. Therefore, the circuit complexity is mainly controlled by the evolution of the squeezing amplitudes. For the benchmark parameters considered here, a positive coupling increases the preparation cost of the scalar Gaussian state but slightly decreases that of the tensor Gaussian state. The scalar sector is therefore more sensitive to the GB coupling, whereas the luminal tensor sector provides a cleaner probe of the pump-field mechanism. Their opposite responses provide a differential state-space diagnostic of the same EGB background.
papers.authors: Tao Li, Hai-Bing Fu, Lei-Hua Liu

papers.title: Haagerup symmetries of the $E_8$ theory and conformal nets at central charge eight
papers.abstract: A Haagerup algebra is a positive strongly rational vertex operator algebra $U$ of central charge eight with $\mathrm{Rep}(U)$ braided equivalent to the Drinfeld center $Z(\cal H_3)$ of the Haagerup fusion category. We prove that $U$ has exactly three holomorphic extensions, each isomorphic to $V_{E_8}$, and that the corresponding Lagrangian algebras have module categories $\cal H_1$, $\cal H_2$ and $\cal H_3$. The extensions attached to $\cal H_2$ and $\cal H_3$ are the two lattice extensions of $V_{E_6 \oplus A_2}$. We prove a recognition theorem for $\cal H_2$ and $\cal H_3$ among unitary fusion categories of rank six with three invertible objects, a noncommutative Grothendieck ring and trivial pointed associator. For simple regular unitary vertex operator algebras with bounded localized vertex operators, we construct the transport module of two ordinary unitary modules when the second integrates in Tener's annular sense. For a unitary conformal Haagerup subalgebra of $V_{E_6 \oplus A_2}$, these results give a completely rational net with representation category $Z(\cal H_3)$, a realization of the Haagerup subfactor and the generalized orbifold of Bischoff. In particular, they apply to the strongly local explicit algebra $S$ of levels $(3,13)$, whose Haagerup property is established in [ArhIII, Theorem 6.1]. In [ArhIII], the net of $S$ is recognized from strong rationality and lattice branching, and a diagonal extension of the net is then used to identify $\mathrm{Rep}(S)$. Here an exact construction of the compatible unitary structure on the diagonal lattice algebra $V_{E_8 \oplus E_8}$, followed by passage to the twin algebra, proves complete unitarity and Condition I+ for every Haagerup algebra. This also gives the VOA--net comparison through smeared vertex operators for unitary conformal embeddings in $V_{E_6 \oplus A_2}$.
papers.authors: C\'edric Arhancet

papers.title: Haagerup vertex operator algebras at central charge eight
papers.abstract:
Evans and Gannon showed that a positive vertex operator algebra of central charge eight whose representation category is the Drinfeld center $Z(\cal H_3)$ of the Haagerup fusion category has one of two character vectors, with six or nineteen currents. Call such an algebra, if strongly rational, a Haagerup algebra. We prove that a Haagerup algebra $U$ has six currents, that $U_1 \cong \mathfrak{sl}_2 \oplus \mathfrak{sl}_2$ embeds into $V_{E_6 \oplus A_2}$ in one of two explicit ways, with levels $(1,39)$ or $(3,13)$, and we determine the lowest weight spaces of its modules and $U_2$ as $U_1$-modules. For the levels $(3,13)$, $U_2$ is one of four Galois conjugate subspaces. Together with $U_1$ it generates the unitary $C_2$-cofinite algebra $S$, which is isomorphic to the algebra constructed by Jiao. For the levels $(1,39)$, $U$ contains the explicit algebra of Riesen. The associated lattice of $U$ is that of the form $x^2+xy+10y^2$, resp.\ $3x^2+3xy+4y^2$, the two classes of the principal genus of discriminant $-39$. Exchanging them in the decomposition of $U$ over its Heisenberg commutant gives a Haagerup algebra $U^
atural$ of the other levels, and $U \mapsto U^
atural$ is a bijection between the isomorphism classes of the two cases. The classification gives exactly two isomorphism classes, forming a single hyperbolic genus, as soon as either explicit candidate is known to be a Haagerup algebra. This property is proved for $S$ in [ArhIII], where the twin $S^
atural$ is also identified, with the algebra of Huang and Riesen, using the results of Dong, Jiao and Xu [DJX26]. The explicit algebras of Jiao and Riesen have rational forms. The proofs combine exact trace relations given by vector-valued modular forms, exact computations in a model of $V_{E_6 \oplus A_2}$, and genera of vertex operator algebras.
papers.authors: C\'edric Arhancet

papers.title: Generalized Frobenius Structures on Hurwitz Spaces, Their Open Extensions and Associated Principal Hierarchies
papers.abstract: We construct generalized Frobenius structures on Hurwitz spaces of arbitrary genus using extended primary differentials. Through contour integrals involving the Cauchy kernel, we derive explicit dispersionless Lax representations for the principal hierarchies of these structures and their almost-dual counterparts. We also construct solutions to the open WDVV equations for both the original and almost-dual structures, and derive explicit principal hierarchies for the resulting rank-one extensions. Finally, we show that these constructions admit Shramchenko deformations.
papers.authors: Shilin Ma

papers.title: Isospectrality breaking in the axial quasinormal modes of Reissner-Nordstr\"om black holes in dynamical Chern-Simons gravity
papers.abstract: We study odd-parity perturbations of Reissner-Nordstr\"om black holes in dynamical Chern-Simons gravity. The dCS action is parity invariant because $\vartheta\,{}^{*}RR$ is the product of two pseudoscalars; nevertheless, the pseudoscalar perturbation has odd parity and enters only the axial sector at linear order and so lifts the axial--polar isospectrality of general relativity. We derive the finite-charge couplings between the pseudoscalar and the axial gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations directly from the linearized field equations. Both directions are governed by the radial kernel $(Mr-Q^2)\Delta/r^8$, and at nonzero charge the pseudoscalar couples to $\Psi+\chi\Psi_e$, with $\chi=2Q/[r\sqrt{(l-1)(l+2)}]$. After diagonalizing the Einstein--Maxwell sector, we compute branch-resolved quasinormal-mode shifts with exterior complex scaling for the photon-sphere modes and Frobenius shooting for the near-extremal zero-damping modes. For the Schwarzschild $l=2$ fundamental mode we obtain $\beta\,\delta\omega=-0.7733-0.3946\,i$ (units $M=\alpha=1$). Off resonance, the gravitational-led shift scales as $\zeta\,l^3$ at $Q=0$ but as $\zeta\,l^2/Q$ at fixed nonzero charge and large $l$. The electromagnetic-led branch becomes exactly degenerate with the pseudoscalar mode at $Q_c=2M\sqrt{l(l+1)+1}/[l(l+1)+2]$, where the pseudoscalar potential coincides with the polar partner of the electromagnetic-led potential; there the breaking is $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt\zeta)$, $M|\Delta\omega|\simeq2.4\sqrt\zeta$ for $l=2$, and the shift reverses sign across $Q_c$. Near extremality the photon-sphere shifts remain finite, whereas the non-degenerate fundamental gravitational-led zero-damping mode is suppressed, $\delta\omega/\omega\simeq6.0\times10^{3}\,\zeta\,(1-Q^2/M^2)$ for $l=2$.
papers.authors: Abhishek Rout

papers.title: Time evolution in the multi-component dynamical Keldysh models
papers.abstract: We construct a time evolution operator for a dynamical quantum models with a multi-component random Gaussian field characterized by a long correlation time.
