We analyze three paradigmatic cases: non-Abelian $SU(2)$ symmetry class for the three-component Gaussian noise and Abelian symmetry classes $U(1)$ and $Z_2$ for the two- and one-component noises correspondingly. Starting with a limiting case of the infinite correlation time (Keldysh model) we shown that statistics of the two-component random field with a non-zero mean is described by the Rice distribution. We derived and solved the system of coupled linear differential equations for the exact diagonal and off-diagonal single-particle Green's functions. We showed how the finite time correlation in Keldysh models are accounted by a continuous fractions method.
papers.authors: M. N. Kiselev

papers.title: Black Hole Entropy from Entangled Quantum Reference Frames
papers.abstract: In the extended phase space of Donnelly and Freidel, the edge modes of a Schwarzschild black hole are dynamical reference frames whose phase space is the cotangent bundle of $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$. Gluing the two exterior regions at the bifurcation point leaves a single canonical pair. Within the extended phase space, this pair can be described either by Kucha\v{r}'s mass and difference of asymptotic times or by the area and the relative rapidity of the two frames, which are two gauge choices of the same system. The latter is the pair of Carlip and Teitelboim, and the relative rapidity is the time shift of the crossed product construction. We quantize the frames in this gauge and construct the gravitational entangling product of the two exteriors. Requiring the frames to be causal restricts them to the semigroup $\mathrm{SL}^+(2,\mathbb{R})$, whose Plancherel measure yields the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy as the entanglement entropy between the two exteriors, together with a logarithmic correction, both independent of the ultraviolet cutoff.
papers.authors: Ludovic Varrin

papers.title: Matrix Samplers and Quantum-Proof Extractors: Their Correspondence and Almost-Optimal Constructions
papers.abstract: We establish an equivalence between matrix samplers and quantum-proof randomness extractors. The classical sampler-extractor equivalence is established by a seminal work of Zuckerman (Random Structures & Algorithms, 1997). Using this equivalence, we construct explicit strong matrix samplers with optimal randomness overhead and near-optimal sample complexity via constructing quantum-proof extractors. Specifically for matrix dimension $D$, accuracy $\varepsilon$ and failure probability $\delta\leq\varepsilon$, our matrix sampler uses $$ m+O_\alpha(\log(D/\delta))\text{ random bits and } O_\alpha\!\left(\varepsilon^{-2-\alpha}\log^{1+\alpha}(D/\delta)\right)\text{ samples}, $$ for any constant $\alpha>0$. Compared with the matrix sampler of Xun and Zuckerman (CCC 2025), our construction has improvements in two aspects. Under optimal random seed length, we can replace the $\operatorname{poly} D$ dependence in the number of samples by $O(\log^{1+\alpha} D)$. Under the same scale of sample size, we can remove their $\log\log D$ factor in the length of the random seed. Our underlying strong quantum-proof extractor has output length $n-O_\alpha(a+\log(1/\eta))$ and seed length at most $(1+\alpha)\log a+(2+\alpha)\log(1/\eta)+O_\alpha(1)$ for $n$-bit sources with conditional min-entropy $n-a$ and error $\eta$. We also obtain strong quantum-proof extractors for every constant entropy rate, for any error as small as $2^{-\Omega(n)}$, having optimal seed length $O(\log(n/\eta))$ and output length $\Omega(n)$, improving previous constructions.
papers.authors: Kuan Cheng, Ruiyang Wu

papers.title: The Symbiosis of Vainshtein and Chameleon Screening
papers.abstract: We present the first study of coexisting Vainshtein and Chameleon screening in cosmic structures. Screening hides fifth forces locally, keeping modified gravity viable. Realistic dark-energy models can activate several mechanisms at once, yet this interplay has been overlooked. We find that (i) the Chameleon resolves the longstanding Galileon void pathology; (ii) it suppresses or eliminates the Vainshtein radius around massive sources; and (iii) the Vainshtein term shrinks the Chameleon's screened core. These effects reshape the observable signatures central to cosmological tests of gravity.
papers.authors: Sergi Sirera, Tessa Baker, Clare Burrage, James Hallam, Krishna Naidoo

papers.title: Perturbative Holonomy Potentials and Vacua in Chiral Supersymmetric Gauge Theories
papers.abstract: We present a Wilsonian framework, globally controlled across the holonomy space, for determining the perturbative data governing the vacua of chiral supersymmetric gauge theories on a circle. This allows lifting the Intriligator--Seiberg classification of semiclassical vacua in 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ Chern--Simons-matter theories to $\mathbb{R}^3\times S^1$. The framework is showcased by finding a rich set of vacuum sectors in a simple U(1) model and by reproducing on flat space the R-twisted reduction (first diagnosed on $S^3\times S^1$) of an SU(2) Maruyoshi--Song theory to the Gang--Yamazaki theory.
papers.authors: Arash Arabi Ardehali

papers.title: Quantum Cryptomania with Classical Communication without One-Way Functions
papers.abstract: In classical cryptography, one-way functions are necessary for most of cryptography. In the quantum world, however, Kretschmer at {TQC'21} and subsequent works have demonstrated that quantum versions of various primitives in minicrypt, such as signatures and private-key encryption, do not require quantum-computable one-way functions (\textsf{qOWF}s). However, the question of the necessity of \textsf{qOWF}s for primitives in Cryptomania like public-key encryption with classical public keys and ciphertexts (\textsf{qPKE}) has remained open. We provide a comprehensive picture of the relationship between \textsf{qPKE} and \textsf{qOWF}. First, our main result is a black-box separation between \textsf{qOWF}s and \textsf{qPKE}. In particular, we show that relative to a unitary, real, and self-inverse oracle, there exists a \textsf{qPKE} scheme (with classical keys and ciphertexts), but \textsf{qOWF}s do not exist. Further, our oracles admit a point-function obfuscation construction, thus ruling out black-box construction of \textsf{qOWF} from point function obfuscations. On the positive side, we construct \textsf{qPKE} from quantum indistinguishability obfuscation for quantum circuits with classical obfuscated descriptions and efficiently verifiable one-way puzzles, which is known to be a potentially weaker assumption than \textsf{qOWF}s, due to an existing black-box separation. Our construction is the quantum analog of the classical construction of \textsf{PKE} from one-way functions and indistinguishability obfuscation in the quantum computation with classical communication (QCCC) setting.
papers.authors: Mohammed Barhoush, Amit Behera

papers.title: The Spectral Edge at Large Central Charge and Black Hole Statistics
papers.abstract: We introduce a new approach to high-energy spectra in AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$, addressing the open challenge of incorporating spectral statistics into the modular bootstrap. Using the analytic theory of $L$-functions attached to two-dimensional CFTs, we leverage modular constraints among high-energy states to derive a sum rule relating the spectral edge to bulk spectral fluctuations. As an application, we establish a refined modular bootstrap bound: letting $\Delta_1$ be the conformal dimension of the lightest excited Virasoro primary of a unitary CFT of central charge $c$, we show that $\Delta_1 - {c-1\over 12} \leq o(c)$, with at most one exceptional value of the scalar gap at each sufficiently large $c$. The result applies to theories with logarithmic rigidity of spectral counting fluctuations, as in random matrix theory. We exhibit circumstances under which the bound is strengthened further.
papers.authors: Eric Perlmutter

papers.title: Rotation slows the instability of Ellis-Bronnikov wormholes
papers.abstract: Rotation weakens the radial instability of Ellis-Bronnikov wormholes in slow-rotation perturbation theory. We investigate its nonlinear effect by evolving stationary rotating drainholes supported by a phantom scalar field. We construct the backgrounds with an independent spectral solver, validate them against published symmetric solutions, and identify a misprint in a published field equation that did not affect the original authors' numerical results. Evolutions perturbed only by discretization error show that rotation slows the collapse. At intermediate spins some throats expand, with the direction of departure depending on the effective perturbation. At the fastest evolved spin, the throat's areal radius shows no growing departure through evolution time $t=150$ in code units, about 28 e-folding times of the static instability, at three resolutions. Two other rapidly rotating models also show no growth over their reliable evolution intervals. Collapsing rotating throats emit an axisymmetric quadrupolar gravitational-wave burst whose energy increases between the two spins compared. Second-order initial data excite the instability through their background truncation error. The results establish slower collapse and prolonged absence of detected radial growth for the sampled asymmetric backgrounds, over finite times from initially axisymmetric data.
papers.authors: Nikita M. Shirokov, Ilya Nachevsky

papers.title: The Standard Model on a finite bosonic lattice with continuum Weyl fermions
papers.abstract: We investigate a formulation of the Standard Model with gauge and Higgs fields regulated on a finite bosonic lattice, while quarks and leptons remain continuum Weyl fermions. This retains the familiar continuum treatment of anomalies, spectral flow, and fermion zero modes. Standard Model anomaly cancellation permits a consistent, gauge-invariant phase for the massless chiral determinant. Yukawa interactions are incorporated with a gauge-covariant spectral cutoff acting on the interaction vertices, not on the fermion propagator. Under the stated analytic conditions, the cutoff can be removed by the local subtractions expected from one-loop power counting, yielding a finite, exactly gauge-invariant functional integral at fixed bosonic lattice spacing and spacetime volume, including topologically nontrivial backgrounds. At zero Yukawa coupling and on smooth weak-field backgrounds, we establish agreement between the appropriately chirality-matched overlap and continuum Weyl fermion determinants up to local counterterms. We also establish reflection positivity at zero Yukawa coupling and zero theta for a modified gauge-field reconstruction; its continuum equivalence with Craig's original reconstruction is not proved. The bosonic continuum limit remains open.
papers.authors: Stephen D. H. Hsu

papers.title: Correlated decoding loses the surface code's effective distance below threshold
papers.abstract: Correlated decoding improves matching and clustering surface-code decoders by reweighting one decoding subgraph conditioned on the other's correction. We show that standard reweighting can cause correlated decoders to fail on size-$(d-1)/2$ fault configurations that a distance-$d$ code should correct, reducing error suppression deep below threshold. Under circuit-level noise, a single first-pass edge can discount several correlated edges, even though their joint occurrence requires additional independent faults, so the decoder favors an over-discounted correction. Regularizing the reweighting rule restores the nominal distance scaling and a clear correlated-decoding advantage.
papers.authors: C\'esar Hernando de la Fuente, Joonas Majaniemi, Evert van Nieuwenburg, Felix Frohnert

papers.title: Transport and thermalization under noncommuting localized constraints
papers.abstract: We investigate the effects of spatially localized conserved quantities on transport and thermalization in quantum and classical many-body systems. We consider several related models: the integrable quantum Volterra model, its nonintegrable classical limit, and two cellular automata derived from the latter. Although localized constraints are often associated with lattice gauge theories, our models do not admit such an interpretation. In systems with discrete degrees of freedom, these constraints induce uniform fragmentation of the Hilbert or configuration space. In the quantum Volterra model, we derive an exact mapping of the dynamics within each Hilbert-space fragment onto a quantum chiral Potts chain. We find that energy transport is ballistic, with identical transport coefficients across all fragments. In the nonintegrable classical limit, energy transport is diffusive, and we similarly find the diffusion constant to be independent of whether or not the constraints are fixed (resolved). Finally, in the cellular automata, we show that, despite leaving transport unaffected, localized constraints lead to a strong breakdown of local ergodicity.
papers.authors: Amir Nesturov, Attila Tak\'acs, Lenart Zadnik

papers.title: Optimal Strategies for Gravitational-Wave Memory Detection with Noise Marginalization in Pulsar Timing Arrays
papers.abstract: Current pulsar timing arrays could detect gravitational wave memory, which would provide a unique test of general relativity. In order to optimize our searches for gravitational wave memory in pulsar timing arrays, we integrate the optimal frequentist statistics for GW memory into the \texttt{enterprise} code suite. We additionally test a noise marginalized version of this statistic, and compare it's effectiveness to the simpler maximum posterior method. We perform these tests on simulated pulsar timing array with red and white noise content, as well as the NANOGrav $15$-year data set. We find no significant variations in our detection statistics between the noise-marginalized and the maximum-posterior methods for the simulated datasets, and only small variations in the NANOGrav $15$-year comparisons. We conclude that for realistic PTAs the noise-marginalization method could be useful for assigning a false alarm probability to Bayesian results, though the maximum posterior method is sufficient for identifying potentially detectable signals.
papers.authors: Rand Burnette, Xavier Siemens

papers.title: Gravitational waves from strong first-order phase transitions in an expanding Universe
papers.abstract: We investigate the gravitational waves generated by first-order phase transitions (PTs) in an expanding Universe. Using a scalar field-fluid coupled model, we perform three-dimensional lattice numerical simulations of slow first-order PTs with strong strength. We observe that the contribution from sound waves to the gravitational wave (GW) signal significantly dominates over that from bubble collisions. The sound wave spectra exhibit two peaks located at the mean bubble separation and the sound-shell width. Rotational modes are generated in the fluid during the bubble collisions, and their magnitude grows with the PT strength ($\alpha$). The effective lifetime of the sound-wave source increases for slower PTs, decreasing for faster PT with larger $\beta/H$ and rising with smaller $\alpha$. While the simulated amplitude of normalized gravitational waves is of order $\mathcal{O}(10^{-2})$, in alignment with Minkowski-spacetime results, the resulting GW spectra differ markedly from those scenarios.
papers.authors: Jintao Zou, Zizhuo Zhao, Yongtao Jia, Ligong Bian

papers.title: Spurious zero-dispersion continua in full $(2,q)$-positivity: A linear hierarchy-depth lower bound from an exactly solvable counting operator
papers.abstract: Variational two-particle reduced-density-matrix methods impose hierarchies of semidefinite constraints. We ask whether a fixed level of such a hierarchy can recover even an elementary many-fermion spectrum, using the dispersion test, in which a value is accepted as an eigenvalue when the minimized dispersion vanishes. We study an exactly solvable operator that counts fermions in one half of the spin orbitals. It is a sum of commuting occupation numbers, so its spectral problem is classical, a Boolean occupation-number problem with integer spectrum, and the obstruction found here is not a genuinely quantum one. We determine the complete set of accepted values at every level of the full hierarchy of particle-hole semidefinite constraints. Besides the integers, this set contains an entire interval of noninteger values unless the hierarchy level grows linearly with the particle number, and we give the exact threshold. The proof constructs explicit q-positive reduced density matrices, diagonal in the occupation basis, by continuing the occupation probabilities of a fixed-particle-number state to a noninteger particle number. The fermionic content is that classical semidefinite constraints on occupation correlations, with nonnegative occupation-pattern probabilities, imply positivity of every particle-hole block, so the noncommuting fermionic conditions remove no false value. A converse argument shows that no other false eigenvalues occur. The limitation is specific to the hierarchy: two-body inequalities that encode the integer spectrum would remove every false value but are not generated at a fixed level. By Erdahl's duality theorem, whose hypotheses we check at fixed particle number, the result applies equally to the full (2,q)-positivity conditions of the constructive solution of the N-representability problem.
papers.authors: Maho Nakata

papers.title: Seifert type magnetohydrostatic equilibria in rotationally symmetric toroidal domains
papers.abstract: We construct magnetohydrostatic equilibria in rotationally symmetric toroidal domains whose magnetic lines define an $(m,n)$ Seifert fibration for arbitrary coprime integers $m,n$.
papers.authors: Daniel Peralta-Salas, Radu Slobodeanu

papers.title: Strict non-tightness of the level-3 quantum bootstrap for a coupled three-dimensional double well, at an excited eigenstate
papers.abstract: For the coupled three-dimensional double well $H=\tfrac12|p|^2+2\sum_i(q_i^2-1)^2-\sum_{i<j}q_i^2q_j^2$ we exhibit, at the first excited energy level (and also at the ground state), a linear functional on polynomials of degree $\le 6$ that satisfies every constraint of the standard level-3 eigenstate bootstrap, has a strictly positive definite moment matrix, and nevertheless assigns a negative value to a nonnegative polynomial. It is therefore an interior point of the level-3 relaxation that is realized by no quantum state. The construction reflects a fact that holds at every level: the eigenstate rows never reach the top-degree momentum moments. At level 3, where strictly feasible points exist, this means that the corresponding block of the moment matrix carries no information about which energies admit one. Every algebraic ingredient is an exact rational certificate, and the only numerical ingredients (spectral enclosures of an eigenfunction) are carried out in rigorous ball arithmetic.
papers.authors: Daniel Keren, Ye Zhou

papers.title: Quantum Algorithms for OPI Variants Beyond Locality and Classical Decodability
papers.abstract: Regev's reduction quantumly finds codewords satisfying nonlinear constraints by decoding the dual code. To date, applications that have not been dequantized have relied on efficient classical decoders and coordinate-wise constraints. We overcome these restrictions separately. Our first contribution uses a quantum decoder to find solutions $\mathbf{y}\in(\mathbb{F}_q\setminus\{0\})^m$ to $\mathbf{B}\mathbf{y}=0$, where $\mathbf{B}\in\mathbb{F}_q^{n\times m}$. For fixed prime $q>2$, Chen, Liu, and Zhandry solve this problem for random matrices with $m=\Omega(n^2)$, a regime now covered by classical algorithms. We adapt their template to codes (spanned by the rows of $\mathbf{B}$) that satisfy a "two-fold multiplication property": the coordinate-wise products of pairs of codewords span a space of dimension smaller than $m$. Under suitable distance conditions, this allows us to solve instances with $m\leq n^{2-\Omega(1)}$, beyond the established guarantees of classical algorithms. We also give an efficient classical algorithm under a stronger three-fold multiplication property, leaving intermediate regimes as candidates for quantum advantage. For Reed-Muller codes punctured at random points, our algorithm finds a word in the unpunctured dual code supported exactly on those points. This works beyond known efficient classical decoding regimes. Our second contribution retains classical decoding but allows global constraints on symbol frequencies. We study "histogram-local" constraints, which specify the allowed numbers of occurrences of each symbol. For broad families, stability under resampling one coordinate yields efficient quantum algorithms for variants of optimal polynomial intersection (OPI) combining coordinate-wise and histogram-local constraints. Adapting Yamakawa-Zhandry, we prove a quantum-classical separation for these problems relative to a classical random oracle.
papers.authors: Seyoon Ragavan, Noah Shutty

papers.title: Teukolsky equations in perturbations of Kerr
papers.abstract: The Kerr stability conjecture has been proved in the slowly rotating case, i.e., $|a|\ll m$, in the sequence of works \cite{KS-GCM1} \cite{KS-GCM2} \cite{KS:Kerr} by Sergiu Klainerman and the author, \cite{GKS22} by Elena Giorgi, Sergiu Klainerman and the author, and \cite{Shen} by Dawei Shen, and extended in \cite{Sze}, by the author, to the full subextremal range $|a|<m$, thereby completing the proof of the Kerr stability conjecture. The proof in \cite{Sze} crucially relies on the two companion papers \cite{MaSz24} \cite{MaSz26} by Siyuan Ma and the author, in which we prove energy-Morawetz estimates respectively for the scalar wave equation and for Teukolsky equations on perturbations of Kerr with $|a|<m$. In addition, two results in \cite{Sze}, concerning the derivation of the Teukolsky wave-transport system in perturbations of Kerr and energy-Morawetz estimates for Teukolsky in the setting of \cite{Sze}, are stated without proofs. The goal of the present paper companion paper to \cite{Sze} is to provide the proof of these two results.
papers.authors: J\'er\'emie Szeftel

papers.title: Kerr stability in the full subextremal range
papers.abstract: In the present paper, we extend the results in the sequence of works \cite{KS-GCM1} \cite{KS-GCM2} \cite{KS:Kerr} by Sergiu Klainerman and the author, \cite{GKS22} by Elena Giorgi, Sergiu Klainerman and the author, and \cite{Shen} by Dawei Shen from the slowly rotating regime $|a|\ll m$ to the full subextremal range $|a|<m$, thereby completing the proof of the Kerr stability conjecture. The restriction $|a|\ll m$ enters in fact only through the estimates for wave equations and for the Bianchi system established in \cite{GKS22}. To remove this restriction, we crucially rely on the two companion papers \cite{MaSz24} \cite{MaSz26} by Siyuan Ma and the author, in which we prove energy-Morawetz estimates respectively for the inhomogeneous scalar wave equation and for inhomogeneous Teukolsky equations on perturbations of Kerr with $|a|<m$. Additionally, some of the results of the present paper are proved in our companion paper \cite{Sze}.
papers.authors: J\'er\'emie Szeftel

papers.title: Cycle Codes and Decoded Quantum Interferometry
papers.abstract: Decoded Quantum Interferometry (DQI) reduces optimization problems with two-variable constraints to decoding cycle codes. For one such problem, namely MaxCut, prior work showed that DQI achieves a nontrivial satisfaction fraction guarantee only on linear-girth graphs, for which MaxCut is classically easy. However, these no-go results rely on minimum distance assumptions that do not represent true decodability thresholds for common noise channels, thus underestimating actual DQI performance. To estimate the true performance, we derive DQI satisfaction guarantees in the presence of imperfect decoding for fixed instances and generalize prior results for random instances. We then study homological cycle codes over arbitrary finite fields and show that minimum-weight decoding is NP-hard for every field of size $q>2$, in contrast with known results for binary cycle codes. On the Linial--Simkin ensemble of regular graphs with logarithmic girth, we prove maximum-likelihood recovery bounds and a strong converse for a family of non-uniform additive noise channels. Moreover, linear programming (LP) decoders provide polynomial-time recovery of a positive fraction of randomly located errors with arbitrary values. These results allow us to prove upper and lower bounds on the approximate optima achievable by DQI when restricted to classical decoders. These bounds rule out quantum advantage in the regimes we analyze but also identify a family of regular Max-$k$-Cut instances on which DQI efficiently achieves a nontrivial satisfaction fraction guarantee.
papers.authors: Anuj Apte, Shouvanik Chakrabarti, Andi Gu, Stephen P. Jordan, Ojas Parekh, Ruslan Shaydulin, Jacob Watkins, Noureldin Yosri, Adam Zalcman

papers.title: Quantum error mitigation from information dynamics
papers.abstract: Overcoming experimental errors is a central challenge in quantum science. This challenge is particularly acute in large and complex quantum circuits, where quantum information spreads into exponentially many paths, foiling any direct attempt to understand errors' impact. In this work, we present a novel approach to understanding and mitigating experimental errors, based on a surprisingly compact representation of a quantum circuit's information dynamics, the reactivity function. The shape of a circuit's reactivity function governs its noise response, and its amenability to different error mitigation methods. From this viewpoint, we introduce two complementary such methods. The first, Pauli-path zero-noise extrapolation, fits a parameterized model to a circuit's reactivity function and uses it to accurately extrapolate to zero noise. The second, tunable error cancellation, filters a circuit's reactivity function to cancel noise on all information up to a threshold locality. Crucially, both methods feature a tuning parameter that allows one to systematically improve their accuracy until convergence. Across three circuit families from published experiments, our methods overcome conventional zero-noise extrapolation biases as large as 30%; at $\sim$$10^{-2}$ root-mean-square error, they reduce sampling cost relative to probabilistic error cancellation by up to a factor of $10^3$.
papers.authors: Philippe Suchsland, Thomas Schuster, Manuel S. Rudolph, Nicholas Noll, Thomas E. O'Brien, Zlatko K. Minev

papers.title: Constraining the Quadratic-mode Amplitude Coupling in GW250114
papers.abstract: Detecting quadratic quasi-normal modes in black hole ringdowns would provide evidence for nonlinear gravitational dynamics, while measuring their properties would enable tests of the corresponding predictions of general relativity. Specifically, second-order black hole perturbation theory predicts that their amplitudes scale with the product of the amplitudes of their parent linear modes, with a coupling coefficient that depends on the spin of the remnant black hole. This mode-specific coupling coefficient has not yet been directly measured from gravitational wave data. Here, we use Bayesian inference on the GW250114 ringdown, modeled with the $220$, $221$, and $220\times220$ modes, to infer the amplitude-coupling coefficient of the $220\times220$ mode. The inferred coefficient is consistent with predictions from numerical relativity fits and second-order perturbation theory; no comparison shows a deviation exceeding $1.3 \sigma$. Although the current data cannot distinguish among these spin-dependent predictions, this measurement establishes a basis for more stringent observational tests of nonlinear gravitational dynamics in black-hole ringdowns.
papers.authors: Yuxin Yang, Changfu Shi, Yi-Ming Hu

papers.title: Asymptotic quasi--local structure induced by Magnetic field
papers.abstract: We introduce a magnetic coherent--state frame over the Landau levels of the two--dimensional Landau Hamiltonian, indexed by a discrete metric space combining spatial and energy degrees of freedom. Although overcomplete, the frame is almost--orthogonal, and we use it to endow the CAR $C^*$--algebra over the one--particle Hilbert space with an \emph{asymptotic quasi--local} (AQL) structure, in which graded commutators of observables localized on disjoint index sets decay exponentially rather than vanish exactly. By means of a family of conditional expectations onto the resulting local subalgebras, we construct a Fr\'echet $*$--subalgebra of almost--local observables, invariant under the discrete group of lattice translations, which act on it by continuous automorphisms. For the full continuous group of magnetic translations we establish a quantitative control on how local observables spread through this almost--local algebra, and we show that this control suffices to extend graded asymptotic abelianness from the lattice to the entire continuous translation group. The results provide a discrete--continuum dictionary intended as the starting point for extending Lieb--Robinson--type techniques from lattice systems to interacting continuum electrons in a magnetic field.
papers.authors: Giuseppe De Nittis

papers.title: Local conservation laws, symmetries and Hamiltonian structure of three-dimensional incompressible Euler flow
papers.abstract: All smooth local conservation laws, symmetries and adjoint symmetries of three-dimensional homogeneous incompressible Euler flow are classified in the primitive velocity--pressure variables. Explicit dependence on time and position and arbitrary finite orders of mixed time and spatial derivatives are allowed. Up to trivial currents, the conservation laws consist of incompressibility, linear and angular momentum, kinetic energy, helicity and generalised time-dependent momentum. Every local adjoint symmetry is represented by a multiplier of these currents. Every finite-order local symmetry is equivalent on solutions to a classical point symmetry, resolving a conjecture of Olver. An explicit local first-order Hamiltonian structure of the primitive system is also established in the geometric theory of partial differential equations. It maps the energy multiplier to time translation; its kernel on local adjoint symmetries is spanned by the helicity and incompressibility multipliers. The proof first excludes higher-order symmetries by comparing their responses to transverse and harmonic characteristic directions in compatible derivative data. The Hamiltonian map and its kernel then determine all local adjoint symmetries from the symmetry classification. Exact multiplier identities and the correspondence between multipliers and current classes complete the conservation-law classification.
papers.authors: Alexey Shevyakov

papers.title: Entangled measurements are necessary for optimal tomography of mixed fermionic Gaussian states and of bosonic Gaussian states near the vacuum
papers.abstract: We prove that learning an unknown mixed fermionic Gaussian state on $m$ modes to trace distance $\epsilon$ requires $\Omega(m^3/\epsilon^2)$ copies when measurements act on one copy at a time, even with arbitrary POVMs, fresh ancillas and classical adaptivity, but without quantum memory between copies. The bound holds for $0<\epsilon\le1/3600$ and separates this model from the known collective rate $\Theta(m^2/\epsilon^2)$. It follows from a uniform single-copy Fisher-information budget and a dimension-independent comparison between trace distance and Gaussian parameters. On covariance matrices of operator norm at most $1-c$, we prove a Frobenius-to-trace-norm continuity bound with constant $[2c(2-c)]^{-1/2}$; matchgate shadows then attain $O(m^3/(c\epsilon^2))$ copies. This also gives explicit error certificates for thermal free-fermion states. For a class of mixed passive bosonic Gaussian states with total mean photon number at most one, a reduction to bounded-block qudit tomography gives a single-copy lower bound $\Omega(m^3/(\epsilon^2\sqrt{\log(m/\epsilon)}))$, versus collective complexity $\Theta(m^2/\epsilon^2)$. These separations answer the mixed-state measurement-resource question posed by Chen et al. A two-mode example has optimal two-copy Fisher trace $5$, versus the separable ceiling $4$. An IBM replication gave a pre-registered witness lower bound $4.12$ at one-sided $95\%$ shot-noise confidence; its interpretation assumes the prescribed preparations and a common measurement channel and does not bound preparation systematics.
papers.authors: Ron Rubin (Rubin Anders Scientific, Inc.)

papers.title: Jordan-like invariant representations of scalar-tensor gravity and the return of imperfect-fluid thermodynamics
papers.abstract: It has been shown that the thermodynamics of frame-invariant scalar-tensor gravity admits an Einstein-frame-like invariant representation, in which the scalar sector is minimally coupled and behaves as a perfect fluid with vanishing temperature. We show that this is not the only invariant thermodynamic organization available. Using instead the invariant matter metric, we construct a Jordan-frame-like invariant representation in which matter is minimally coupled and the gravitational action takes the Brans-Dicke-Bergmann-Wagoner form with invariant fields $\Psi=\mathcal I_1^{-1}$, $\mathcal U(\Psi)$, and $\omega_{\mathrm{inv}}(\Psi)$. In this representation the metric field equations retain the Hessian sector characteristic of Jordan-frame scalar-tensor gravity. A $1+3$ decomposition of the corresponding effective stress tensor yields nonvanishing heat flux and anisotropic stress in a generic congruence. In the $\Psi$-comoving frame, the usual first-order thermodynamic identifications are recovered in invariant form, including $K_{\mathrm J}T_{\mathrm J}=-\dot\Psi/(\kappa^2\Psi)$ and $\eta_{\mathrm J}=\dot\Psi/(2\kappa^2\Psi)$, with the bulk channel obtained in homogeneous and isotropic sectors. Thus, frame-invariant scalar-tensor thermodynamics is not intrinsically restricted to an Einstein-frame-like perfect-fluid description: it also admits a Jordan-frame-like invariant formulation in which the effective imperfect-fluid interpretation is manifest.
papers.authors: David S. Pereira, Jos\'e Pedro Mimoso

papers.title: qdmag: A Python package for simulating nonequilibrium magnetization of molecules using quantum master equations
papers.abstract: We present qdmag, a computational utility for calculating the magnetization of magnetic molecules in a time-varying external magnetic field by solving a generalized Lindblad quantum master equation with spin-phonon coupling treated as a dissipation term. The package relies on the spin Hamiltonian formalism, which includes both the magnetic exchange interactions and the zero-field splitting (ZFS) interaction. Different types of magnetic exchange interaction and ZFS terms up to 12th order, which are written in terms of the extended Stevens operators, are supported. qdmag enables long-time evolution of magnetization for up to a few milliseconds, which is achieved through a staircase approximation of the magnetic field as a function of time. For high-dimensional spin Hamiltonians, a lower-dimensional effective Hamiltonian is constructed to make the calculations computationally feasible. Three case studies of one-spin, two-spin, and three-spin systems are presented to demonstrate the usage of qdmag. Our work offers a computational tool to bridge the gap between theoretical development and numerical calculations of spin dynamics in the presence of spin-phonon coupling.
papers.authors: Shuanglong Liu, Xiao Chen, Andrew Cupo, James N. Fry, Hai-Ping Cheng

papers.title: Periodic Orbits of Van der Waals Black Holes
papers.abstract: Black holes in asymptotically anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetime whose extended-phase-space thermodynamics reproduces that of a van der Waals fluid exactly form a distinctive class, the van der Waals black holes (VBHs). The timelike geodesics of VBHs are solved, their periodic orbits are catalogued, and the gravitational waves emitted along them are computed, so as to trace how the thermodynamic pressure P and the molecular-volume parameter b shape the orbital dynamics. Integrating the geodesic equations numerically yields the energy, angular momentum and radius of the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) and maps out the family of bound orbits. To delimit the parameter window in which the effective potential stays well behaved, we introduce a critical angular momentum Ls. Within the orbit-classification scheme, we compute the energies corresponding to rational q for several parameter sets and display the resulting orbits. The waveforms produced along these orbits are generated within the "Kludge" formalism, which makes it possible to quantify the imprint of b on the wave amplitude and on the period. Both the orbital architecture and the gravitational-wave signature turn out to be strongly sensitive to b. The dynamical behavior of VBHs and Schwarzschild-AdS (SAdS) black holes differs markedly, providing a new perspective for probing black hole thermodynamics via gravitational wave observations.
papers.authors: Xuyao Gong, Zhaoyi Xu, Meirong Tang

papers.title: Thermodynamic Representations of Algebraically Modified FLRW Dynamics at the Apparent Horizon
papers.abstract: We investigate the thermodynamic description of a general class of algebraically modified Friedmann dynamics in which the physical matter obeys the standard conservation equation and the modification is encoded through a function \(g(\rho)\). By introducing a thermodynamic matter representation \(\chi(\rho)\), we construct the corresponding matter variables, heat flow, work term, and horizon entropy, and show that both the Clausius relation and the first-law balance can be consistently maintained. A continuous family of representations is then defined by \(\chi_\lambda(\rho)=(1-\lambda)\rho+\lambda g(\rho)\) with \(0\leq\lambda\leq1\), and the physical-matter and effective-fluid descriptions as the two endpoints. The associated thermodynamic quantities transform consistently between these limits. We further show that apparent departures from equilibrium can arise from mixing quantities belonging to different representations, rather than from a genuine non-equilibrium entropy-production mechanism. These results identify a continuous freedom of thermodynamic representation within this class of modified FLRW dynamics.
papers.authors: Xiao Liu

papers.title: Dimensional reduction and thermodynamics of a non-local scalar field theory
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the dimensional reduction of a non-local scalar field theory from $1+3$ to $1+2$ dimensions. The bulk theory is governed by an entire-function non-local form factor $e^{-\Box_E/\Lambda^2}$, where $\Lambda$ sets a fundamental high-energy scale. By constraining external classical sources to a bidimensional plane, we perform the exact dimensional reduction, derive the effective planar Green's function in terms of the complementary error function, and propose the corresponding effective non-local pseudo-differential planar Lagrangian. Using the static propagator, we determine the interaction energy between two point-like planar charges, proving that the non-local scale regularizes the short-distance singularity at the origin while smoothly recovering the standard Yukawa potential at long distances. Furthermore, we obtain the retarded, advanced, and Feynman Green's functions in coordinate space, demonstrating that macroscopic causality and tree-level unitarity are preserved. Finally, implementing the Matsubara formalism, we investigate the finite-temperature regime and evaluate the exact thermal free energy, pressure, entropy, and heat capacity. We show that the effective planar theory exhibits a fractional effective number of degrees of freedom ($g_{\rm eff}=1/2$ for $m \ll T \ll \Lambda$, crossing over to $g_{\rm eff}=1$ for $T \gg \Lambda$) originating from kinematic bulk leakage and that pressure, entropy, and heat capacity remain positive at all temperatures.
papers.authors: S. Duque Cesar, M. J. Neves

papers.title: Tidal Love numbers of wormholes as black-hole mimickers
papers.abstract: We study the dynamical scalar tidal Love numbers of wormholes that provide viable mimickers for black holes, focusing on thin-shell Schwarzschild and Damour-Solodukhin geometries. Using a matched near- and far-zone expansion, we determine their tidal response in the low-frequency regime. The presence of a long throat introduces an additional characteristic scale and naturally separates the modes into two classes. Super-throat modes probe the global wormhole geometry and are sensitive to both asymptotic regions, whereas sub-throat modes probe only one side of the wormhole and effectively perceive the throat as a black-hole horizon. We derive the scalar tidal Love numbers analytically for both classes of modes and show that their dissipative parts exhibit distinct low-frequency behavior, reflecting whether one or both potential barriers participate in the scattering process. We further find that, as the wormhole approaches the black-hole limit, the super-throat contribution becomes progressively negligible, while the sub-throat response smoothly reduces to that of a Schwarzschild black hole. These results demonstrate that the tidal response of wormholes depends crucially on whether the perturbation probes the global structure of the throat.
papers.authors: Sergey N. Solodukhin, Vagif Tagiev

papers.title: Revealing the Quantum Signature of Gravity via Gravitational Waves
papers.abstract: Can propagating gravitational waves serve as operational probes of the quantum nature of gravity? We address this question by developing a unified theoretical framework that combines spacetime geometry, quantum information, and gravitational-wave physics. Starting from the geodesic deviation equation in linearized General Relativity, we derive the effective detector Hamiltonian directly from spacetime geometry and construct the complete quantum dynamics for detector subsystems interacting with both classical and quantized propagating gravitational-wave fields. This unified formulation enables a direct comparison between classical and quantum descriptions of gravitational radiation within the same physical framework. We demonstrate that classical gravitational-wave backgrounds can induce mixedness in the detector state but cannot generate genuine quantum correlations between the detector subsystems. In contrast, quantized gravitational waves coherently mediate gravity-induced entanglement, quantum coherence, quantum memory, and nonclassical correlations, providing clear operational signatures of the quantum nature of propagating gravitational radiation. We further discuss how mesoscopic quantum mechanical oscillators offer a promising route towards experimentally probing these effects. Our results establish a geometric and quantum-information-based framework for exploring quantum gravity through propagating gravitational waves.
papers.authors: Partha Nandi

papers.title: Analytic motions of spinning particles in Schwarzschild-(anti-)de Sitter spacetime
papers.abstract: The motion of a spinning test particle in a static, spherically symmetric spacetime with a cosmological constant is studied within the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon formalism, working to linear order in the particle's spin. By exploiting the symmetries of the background, the radial and latitudinal dynamics are reduced to first-order equations governed by a spin-deformed quintic polynomial. A complete classification of the real root structure of this quintic is carried out, from which the allowed orbital types for spinning particles in the Schwarzschild-anti-de Sitter and Schwarzschild-de Sitter geometries follow directly. The parameter dependence of the root structure and of the stable circular orbit interval is analyzed. In particular, for values of the cosmological constant beyond the Stuchl\'ik limit, where spinless particles admit no bound orbits, spinning particles can still remain bound. The radial motion is expressed piecewise in terms of Lauricella hypergeometric functions, with the simple positive real roots of the quintic acting as branch cuts. The latitudinal motion consists of small oscillations about an equatorial plane, and its phase, governed by the same quintic, admits an analogous analytic representation.
papers.authors: Rui-Hui Lin, Xing-You Zhou, Chao-Jun Feng

papers.title: Multimode squeezed light generation and characterization
papers.abstract: Nowadays, the realization of quantum computations and communications based on continuous variables has attracted significant attention due to a substantial expansion of the system dimensionality. The main progress in this area is attributed to the implementation of multimode systems based on squeezed states of light. One of the simplest ways to generate such states relies upon their producing in a single-pass optical parametric amplifier (OPA) under ultrafast pumping. However, for homodyne detection of such multimode states, the profile of the local oscillator (LO) must perfectly match the profile of the measured mode. Usually, this is not the case; therefore, a proper treatment of multimode squeezing is required. In this work, we study both theoretically and experimentally the multimode squeezed light generated in type-0 and type-II OPA. We characterize such sources using the Schmidt-mode representation and investigate the degree of squeezing depending on the LO spectral profile, employing a pulse shaping technique. In addition, we investigate cluster states that can be generated under the given experimental conditions. This work might have a significant impact on the realization of multimode quantum protocols.
papers.authors: Alexander Chudakov, Vladislav Severin, Anastasia Poshevkina, Danil Malyshev, Kirill Kuznetsov, Olga Tikhonova, Dmitry Kalashnikov, Polina R. Sharapova

papers.title: Wormhole-induced gravi-axion mass distributions and the second-harmonic crossover
papers.abstract: We compute the distribution of the wormhole-induced gravi-axion curvature mass across baby-universe sectors when the first two harmonics are retained. For independent complex Gaussian coefficients, with an optional displacement of the first channel, an exact global-minimum condition gives the mass distribution and its threshold coefficient. At fixed nonzero second-harmonic width, the cumulative probability below mass $M$ scales as $M^5$. For a weak second harmonic, the unit-harmonic $M^4$ behavior is recovered in an intermediate low-mass range above the crossover scale. We also distinguish the actual relative mass-squared error from the probability that a phase-independent bound fails to certify the unit-harmonic approximation. In the common-background quadratic correlator with unit residues, the lower threshold remains zero and the two-harmonic tail produces an $s^{3/2}$ nonanalytic term in the Euclidean momentum squared $s$. The results are conditional on the chosen state and effective wormhole coefficients.
papers.authors: Amin Rezaei Akbarieh

papers.title: Best Annealing Path of Simulated Quantum Annealing via Efficient Adiabatic Phase Transition
papers.abstract: Nested Simulated Annealing (NSA) is proposed for accelerating the classical simulation of Quantum Annealing (QA). NSA is based on two-spin interaction and exploits the causality of spin-flip, thereby significantly reducing computational cost. And through Unitary Coupled-Cluster (UCC) method, I establish a connection between NSA and XX interaction which is one of non-stoquastic Hamiltonians and demonstrate that NSA effectively utilizes a trivial degenerate state. Furthermore, by treating spins as continuous variables, I derive an energy formulation that incorporates both the problem Hamiltonian and the perturbation Hamiltonian induced by transverse electromagnetic field and show that the annealing path characterized by the lowest local-maximum exhibits the fastest convergence. Based on the result, I present a strategy for finding optimal annealing parameters for Simulated Quantum Annealing (SQA).
papers.authors: Kiyotaka Murashima

papers.title: Exact dynamics of spinning particles and the spin wall in Schwarzschild spacetime
papers.abstract: The motion of a spinning test body is governed by the Mathisson--Papapetrou--Dixon equations and deviates from geodesics already at first order in the spin. Most studies of this problem truncate the dynamics at linear order; here we solve the equatorial, spin-aligned problem in Schwarzschild spacetime at all orders in the spin under the Tulczyjew--Dixon condition. Eliminating the four-velocity casts the system into a closed algebraic form and reduces the motion to a single first-order radial equation. Keeping track of both kinematical masses, the norm of the four-momentum and its projection on the velocity, we find that the representative worldline ceases to be timelike on a surface in the space of radius, spin and angular momentum. We call this surface the spin wall. It bounds the radii accessible to a spinning body and is present for every nonvanishing value of the momentum's angular component; only for the purely radial family does it collapse, and that family moves on a geodesic. Its position follows in closed form and may lie inside the horizon, enclose it, or reach the exterior, the last possibility arising already at small spin. We also examine how far the pole--dipole truncation remains under control where the wall is accessible. Within that regime we determine the circular orbits and their stability, the spin dependence of the marginally stable orbit, and the perihelion advance beyond first order in the spin.
papers.authors: Chao-Jun Feng, Rui-Hui Lin

papers.title: Exact quantum geometry from sublattice symmetry: Closed-form solution of the quarter-flux Harper-Hofstadter model
papers.abstract: Quantum geometry has emerged as a guiding principle across atomic and condensed-matter physics, shaping the topological responses of Bloch bands and the stability of the correlated phases they host. Sublattice symmetry, though common among bipartite lattice models, has not yet been exploited to obtain closed-form quantum geometry in multiband systems. For this purpose, we derive a general expression for the QGT of sublattice-symmetric systems in terms of contributions from the individual sublattice sectors, and show that this symmetry renders the Bloch Hamiltonian of a paradigmatic four-band model, the quarter-flux Harper-Hofstadter model, anti-block-diagonal, analytically yielding the spectrum, eigenstates, and full quantum geometric tensor (QGT), including the Berry curvature and quantum metric, for all four bands. The model, describing charged particles on a two-dimensional square lattice subjected to a uniform magnetic field, has recently been realized experimentally with ultracold atoms, photons, and superconducting circuits. Finally, we evaluate fractional-Chern-insulator stability criteria analytically and quantify the lowest band of the quarter-flux Harper-Hofstadter model to be a nearly ideal Chern band. Our approach opens a route for studying also the quantum geometry of other sublattice-symmetric multiband systems.
papers.authors: Isaac Tesfaye, Andr\'e Eckardt

papers.title: A Note on a High-Energy Limit of Gravitational Perturbation Theory
papers.abstract: The post-Minkowskian expansion of general relativity expands the metric in Newton's constant G around flat space-time, but much effort currently focuses on ways to extend its range of applicability by summing the perturbative series to all orders. A regime of particular interest is a specific high-energy limit where a formula derived recently provides the momentum kick of binary scattering problem to all orders, and even suggests an approach towards strong coupling. We show that this is an asymptotic expansion. Although the series diverges we give evidence that it is Borel summable, and the full function in integral form is finite. As a by-product we determine the transcendentality properties of the coefficients in the expanded expression.
papers.authors: Poul H. Damgaard, Ludovic Plante

papers.title: Kerr Quasinormal Modes without Variable Separation: A Two-Dimensional Hyperboloidal Teukolsky Solver with Physics-Informed Neural Networks
papers.abstract: We use physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) to solve the gravitational quasinormal-mode (QNM) eigenvalue problem for Kerr spacetime directly in the two-dimensional hyperboloidal formulation of the Teukolsky equation. This formulation does not require separation of variables and thus retains the coupled radial--angular structure. Such a scheme provides a prototype for calculating the QNMs of beyond-Kerr black holes for which the perturbation equations are non-separable. Sequences with increasing angular momentum are constructed, reaching close to the extremal limit. We focus on the fundamental modes $(\ell,m,n)=(2,0,0)$, $(2,1,0)$, $(2,2,0)$, $(3,3,0)$ and $(4,4,0)$, together with the first two overtones $(2,2,1)$ and $(2,2,2)$. After training, the frequency at every spin is refined by solving the discretized equation for it, so that it depends much less on where the stochastic training happens to stop. Comparison with continued-fraction values shows that every reported real and imaginary frequency component of the production network remains below $0.23\%$ error, with a median deviation of $2\times10^{-4}\%$. For the fundamental modes, both components agree within about $10^{-3}\%$ up to $a/M=0.97$, and the real parts within $5\times10^{-4}\%$ at every spin. Sub-percent accuracy is maintained in the near-extremal regime, where the damping rate becomes small and the modes are longest-lived; there the damping errors grow, and the largest, $0.23\%$, belongs to the $(2,2,1)$ overtone. The results establish a non-spectral numerical route to multidimensional black-hole perturbation eigenproblems which does not match the substantially higher precision of dedicated Kerr solvers but offers greater flexibility and requires less analytical pre-processing. The proposed approach is designed to be applicable to other backgrounds whose perturbation equations do not separate.
papers.authors: Antonio Ferrer-S\'anchez, Daniela D. Doneva, Jos\'e D. Mart\'in-Guerrero, Stoytcho S. Yazadjiev, Roberto Ruiz de Austri-Bazan, Yolanda Vives-Gilabert, Jos\'e A. Font

papers.title: Hidden transverse-flow topology in partially coherent structured light
papers.abstract: Partial coherence is commonly viewed as a mechanism that reduces contrast or smooths intensity structure. Here we show that it can also encode hidden transverse-flow topology. Starting from the cross-spectral density, we formulate a generalized transverse flux, an effective velocity field, and the associated flux trajectories for quasi-monochromatic partially coherent paraxial beams. This construction converts two-point correlation phases into local transport information and reduces to the usual coherent energy-flow picture in the single-mode limit. Because the generalized flux is obtained through a local differential operation on the cross-spectral density, the proposed trajectories are, in principle, reconstructible from sufficiently resolved phase-sensitive measurements of the complex second-order coherence function, subject to the regularization required by numerical differentiation. Two analytical beam families expose this hidden topology. In twisted Gaussian Schell-model beams, a Gaussian intensity hides a distributed rotational flow with nonzero vorticity. In Laguerre-Christoffel-Darboux beams, sources with identical intensity profiles can have different flux topology, producing either spiral or purely radial trajectories. Thus, intensity and coherence magnitude do not exhaust the physical information contained in the cross-spectral density: partial coherence can reorganize the hidden topology of transverse optical transport.
papers.authors: Rosario Mart\'inez-Herrero, \'Angel S. Sanz

papers.title: On the nature of oscillating modes of proto-neutron stars
papers.abstract: Newborn proto-neutron stars (PNS) are potential targets of gravitational wave asteroseismology, the study of the (inner) structure of stars via their oscillation modes. To prepare for the eventual detection of such modes by current and future gravitational wave observatories, theoretical studies have obtained the possible spectrum of oscillations. However, there has been disagreement when it comes to identifying and classifying specific modes according to the physical mechanism that excites them. In this paper, we present a novel scheme to classify the oscillation modes of a newly born PNS surrounded by a stalled accretion shock in core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe). Our classification is physically motivated, as it is based on the energy of the restoring forces of the mode. We investigate the nature of the modes by considering the different regions of the CCSN that they stem from. We apply this scheme to a set of 28 non-rotating 1D, 2D and 3D CCSN simulations performed with two different numerical codes and using different progenitors and equations of state. In that way, we find that there are different families of f-, p- and g-modes in the system, living in different areas. More specifically, we identify two families of f- and p-modes associated with the PNS and the shock, respectively, and two families of g-modes originating from the two convectively stable regions, one in the PNS core and one near its surface. We also find that the dominant high-frequency emission mode is the f-mode of the PNS, associated with the strong density gradient at its surface. Our classification procedure is automatic, performs consistently for all the models considered, and paves the way to systematic studies of the dependence of the mode frequencies on the PNS properties, with direct application to parameter estimation from future observations of gravitational wave signals.
papers.authors: Dimitra Tseneklidou, Alejandro Torres-Forne, Pablo Cerda-Duran, Martin Obergaulinger, Jose Antonio Font

papers.title: Perturbative Dissipation in Minimal Warm Inflation
papers.abstract: We present an analysis of the perturbative modes of dissipation in the minimal warm inflation model where an axion-inflaton is coupled to a gluon thermal bath through the axion-gauge coupling. The corresponding friction coefficient, which generically is governed by IR physics, for the processes we consider is dominated by Landau damping of soft space-like gluons and the plasmon decay of hard on shell gluons. Since both of these processes are IR dominated, the friction coefficient becomes sensitive to the non-perturbative magnetic mass scale $m_{g}^{-1} \sim (\alpha T)^{-1}$ which in turn leads to the friction coefficient's overall linear proportionality to $\alpha$, which is much less suppressed in $\alpha$ powers compared to the well understood term from Chern-Simons (CS) diffusion $(\propto \alpha^5)$. On the other hand, this contribution to the friction coefficient is suppressed due to slow roll. We show that this can be viewed as a suppression of local spontaneous CPT violation for derivative couplings in general and that time correlations of nonlocal variables which do not fall off at large time separations are what allow an unsuppressed friction coefficient.
papers.authors: Daniel J. H. Chung, Nidhi Sudhir, Lian-Tao Wang

papers.title: New Universal Relations for Magnetized Neutron Stars
papers.abstract: Unlike the neutron-star mass--radius relation, which depends sensitively on the internal stellar structure through the equation of state of dense nuclear matter, certain neutron-star properties obey approximately universal relations that exhibit only weak dependence on the equation of state. In this paper, we explore new universal relations for magnetized neutron stars. We focus on a purely poloidal dipolar magnetic-field configuration and treat the effects of the magnetic field perturbatively to second order in the field strength. After appropriately normalizing the relevant quantities by the stellar mass and the magnetic-field strength at the pole, we first identify an exact universal relation between the magnetic dipole moment and stellar compactness. We then find approximate universal relations among the magnetic dipole moment, magnetically-induced stellar quadrupole moment, and ellipticity, with fractional variations due to the equation of state at the level of O(10%). We support these numerical findings with analytic estimates for Newtonian polytropes, which reproduce the observed behavior. Among the newly discovered relations, the one connecting the magnetic dipole moment and stellar quadrupole moment may be particularly useful for the analysis of gravitational-wave signals from binaries containing magnetized neutron stars.
papers.authors: Byon N. Jayawiguna, Siddarth Ajith, Takuya Katagiri, Kent Yagi, Piyabut Burikham

papers.title: Schr\"{o}dinger Generator for High-Dimensional Integration and Sampling on Quantum Many-Body States
papers.abstract: Integration and sampling in high dimensions are among central challenges in modern science and technology, underlying applications ranging from quantum many-body physics to Bayesian inference and artificial intelligence. Although conventional Monte Carlo methods are formally scalable, their efficiency deteriorates rapidly in the presence of strong correlations or sharp features in high-dimensional configuration space. Here we introduce a new framework, termed the Schr"odinger Generator, for integration and sampling based on the explicit optimization of coordinate transformations. The method decomposes the total Jacobian into two complementary components, including an adaptive map that minimizes estimator variance by learning the marginal structure in each dimension, and a normalizing-flow-based transformation that captures non-factorizable correlations in the target distribution. A final resampling step guarantees unbiased sampling even when the learned transformation is imperfect. We demonstrate stable and scalable performance for nuclear quantum many-body states in dimensions exceeding 600. Short-range correlations among nucleons in finite nucleus are faithfully reproduced. The framework offers a physically transparent approach to high-dimensional stochastic integration and sampling, opening new possibilities for simulations of complex quantum systems.
papers.authors: Lin-Jing Jiang, Fu Ma, Pei Li, Kai-Jia Sun, Guo-Liang Ma, Yu-Gang Ma

papers.title: Residual Galactic binary foreground in LISA stochastic gravitational-wave background inference: source power concentration and spectral degeneracy
papers.abstract: Galactic compact binaries are expected to form a dominant millihertz foreground for the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA), and residual foreground power can bias stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB) inference or increase its uncertainty. Using the LISA Data Challenge 2A (LDC2A) injections and the Erebor injection-recovery match, we construct a catalog residual spectrum from 0.4 to 6.0 mHz. We distinguish two effects. The first is the departure from Gaussianity of a sum of source signals with independent random phases, quantified by its excess kurtosis; the second is the spectral degeneracy between the residual and the SGWB in the mean binned power. Source discreteness determines the excess kurtosis of this sum, but instrumental noise and fiducial SGWB power strongly reduce its magnitude in most bins. We quantify this degeneracy with a local Fisher information matrix for the SGWB amplitude $\Omega_0$ and the residual-power factor $\beta$. For a frequency-independent SGWB with $\Omega_0=10^{-11}$ and residual power distributed uniformly over the Fourier frequencies within each bin, marginalizing over $\beta$ increases the $\Omega_0$ uncertainty by $13.6\%$ with the Gaussian Fourier-amplitude covariance and by $13.8\%$ with the finite-source diagonal random-phase covariance. Under the Gaussian Fourier-amplitude covariance, the largest allowed prior standard deviation on $\beta$ that limits this increase to $10\%$ is $0.0073$. With this covariance recomputed at each fiducial amplitude, the uncertainty increase ranges from $12.7\%$ to $20.7\%$ over $10^{-13}\leq\Omega_0\leq10^{-10}$. The residual-SGWB spectral degeneracy persists under alternative distributions of residual power over Fourier frequencies and diagonal covariances, while omitting the residual induces a systematic bias in the fitted SGWB amplitude.
papers.authors: Ruo-Yu Guan, Yan Wang

papers.title: A Kernel-Based Density of States Estimator for Quantum Computing
papers.abstract: We introduce a quantum kernel method for estimating the density of states (DoS) of quantum many-body systems. The method exploits the Rodeo algorithm as a physical implementation, requiring no modification of its standard single-ancilla circuit. Averaging the Rodeo response over Haar-random input states reconstructs the DoS convolved with a spectral kernel whose analytical form is determined entirely by the probability distribution of the sampled evolution times. This establishes a direct quantum analogue of the classical Kernel Polynomial Method (KPM): Haar-random states perform stochastic trace estimation, while the temporal sampling distribution plays the role of the reconstruction kernel. We derive the estimator, quantify its statistical and systematic uncertainties, and establish an explicit correspondence between quantum reconstruction kernels and classical signal-processing window functions, enabling concepts such as spectral leakage, side-lobe attenuation, and main-lobe width to guide kernel design. The method is validated numerically on the one-dimensional transverse-field spin--$\sfrac{1}{2}$ and spin--$1$ Ising models, where the reconstructed density of states and the resulting thermodynamic observables agree with exact diagonalization within the estimated statistical uncertainties.
papers.authors: Julio Cesar Siqueira Rocha

papers.title: Unconditional Unclonable Encryption
papers.abstract: We give an unconditional construction of information-theoretically secure one-time private-key unclonable encryption for one-bit messages, with efficient encryption and decryption and exponentially small unclonable-indistinguishability advantage. Previous work by Bhattacharyya and Culf (Nature Physics, 2026) and Bhattacharyya, Broadbent, and Culf (arXiv:2603.08916) either only showed inverse-polynomial security loss or required inefficient encryption/decryption operations; we avoid both of these caveats. Our scheme's key is a uniformly random non-identity phase-free Pauli on $n$ qubits, and bit $a$ is encrypted as a random $(-1)^a$ eigenstate of that Pauli. We prove that the probability that both receivers recover the bit is at most $1/2 + O\left(2^{-n/2}\right).$ By a lower bound due to Broadbent, Culf, and Rochette (IACR Communications in Cryptology, 2026), this is the best probability bound achievable with $n$-qubit ciphertexts while ensuring perfect correctness (up to the constant hidden in the $O(\cdot)$).
papers.authors: Prabhanjan Ananth, Seyoon Ragavan, Amit Sahai

papers.title: A Physically-Realisable Quantum Programming Language with Quantum-Controlled Quantum Channels
papers.abstract: In contrast to a classical bit, which can only take the value $0$ or $1$, its quantum counterpart---a qubit---can exist in a superposition of $0$ and $1$. This is a superposition of data values, and it is then tempting to superpose programs as well. Indeed, a particular superposition of programs, known as the quantum SWITCH, has attracted considerable attention. A natural way to superpose programs is conditional branching on quantum data, and several studies have pursued this idea. However, there is a well-known semantic difficulty with this approach, and the fundamental question of whether the languages proposed in prior work can be physically realised remains open. This paper proposes a physically realisable quantum programming language with quantum branching over quantum channels. We first analyse the semantic difficulty from an implementation perspective and show that the difficulty is caused by arbitrariness in the implementation. We then design a language that is free from this arbitrariness. As expected from its implementation-oriented design, our language is physically realisable. We argue for this from two directions: first, we give a method for compiling programs into quantum circuits; and second, we show that our programs stay within the physically admissible range, namely, that they neither yield probabilities greater than one nor violate causal inequalities. The absence of such violations is established through the inclusion of our language in QC-QC, a notion of realisability studied in physics.
papers.authors: Kengo Hirata, Takeshi Tsukada

papers.title: Quantum-classical crossover in finite spin-1/2 rings with Dzyaloshinsky-Moriya interaction
papers.abstract: We study finite spin-$\tfrac12$ rings with nearest-neighbor Heisenberg exchange, Dzyaloshinsky-Moriya interaction, and an external magnetic field. We introduce a phenomenological interpolation parameter between the fully quantum Hamiltonian and a state-dependent mean-field description. Using dissipative Gisin-Schr\"odinger dynamics, we analyze the resulting quantum-classical crossover through local magnetization, connected spin correlations, single-site entropy, and the saturation field of the fully polarized state.
papers.authors: Ra\'ul S\'anchez Gal\'an, Robert Wieser

papers.title: Transferred QAOA Parameters Remember the Penalty Scale: A $\lambda$-Resonance Law for Constrained Quantum Optimization
papers.abstract: Training the variational angles of the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm once on a small instance and reusing them on larger ones, known as parameter transfer, is the standard route past the exact-simulation wall. Existing literature explains its success almost entirely through structural similarity. We identify a new, independent axis that governs transfer whenever constraints are encoded as penalties: the trained angles memorize the penalty weight $\lambda$ of their training instance. For any scalarized cost function with an integer-valued violation count, we prove that at arbitrary fixed QAOA angles $(\beta,\gamma)$ of depth $p$, the probability mass $F(\lambda)$ on the feasible subspace is a finite real trigonometric polynomial in $\lambda$ whose angular frequencies lie on an integer lattice generated by the trained $\gamma$'s. Three consequences follow immediately: transfer feasibility is a resonance peaked where the deployment penalty matches the training penalty; the resonance width scales as $1/(v_{max}\sum_k|\gamma_k|)$, so low-$|\gamma|$ angle sets are systematically more transferable; and the curve exhibits revival peaks at spacings $2\pi/\gamma_k$. We confirm all three predictions by exact statevector experiments on a 20-qubit multi-user resource-allocation QUBO. The theorem is independent of how the angles were obtained and applies to any integer-penalty QUBO, recasting a widely reported failure mode of penalty-based QAOA as deterministic, predictable phase interference rather than an energetic tuning problem.
papers.authors: Krit Grover

papers.title: Depth-reduced quantum simulation of Lindbladian dynamics via adaptive variational quantum trajectory compression
papers.abstract: Quantum simulation of open quantum systems in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) era is hindered by the non-unitary nature of dissipative dynamics and the limited quantum resources available on near-term quantum processors, namely restricted qubit counts and noise-limited circuit depths. In this work, we propose an efficient quantum algorithm for simulating Lindbladian dynamics on NISQ devices. For open quantum systems with Pauli dissipations, we first derive a compact and stable mixed-unitary adjoint channel that approximates the target dissipative dynamics and enables ancilla-free implementation through trajectory sampling. To further reduce the circuit depth required for implementing the sampled trajectories, we introduce an adaptive variational quantum trajectory compression framework. In this framework, a depth-adaptive parameterized quantum circuit is trained to approximate repeated Hamiltonian simulation operators, which are then used to replace repeated unitary segments appearing in the sampled trajectories. Importantly, the training procedure can also be performed without auxiliary qubits. Numerical simulations of the dissipative quantum $XY$ model and the interacting disordered $XXZ$ chain demonstrate the accuracy and reduced execution gate counts of the proposed algorithm. Our results provide a practical route toward ancilla-free and depth-reduced simulation of open quantum systems on near-term quantum hardware.
papers.authors: Huan-Yu Liu, Cheng Xue, Yun-Jie Wang, Xi-Ning Zhuang, Chao Wang, Yu-Chun Wu, Zhao-Yun Chen, Guo-Ping Guo

papers.title: Probing Rotating Einstein-Power-Yang-Mills Black Holes through Shadows and Quasinormal Modes: Prospects for Event Horizon Telescope Constraints
papers.abstract: Within Einstein power-Yang-Mills gravity (EPYM), we build a rotating black hole via the Newman-Janis procedure applied to the spherically symmetric static seed, obtaining an EPYM-inspired Kerr-like metric controlled by the spin \(a\), the magnetic Yang-Mills charge \(Q\), and the power parameter \(q\). We analyse the horizon structure and the photon region, and we compute the shadow as it appears to a remote observer for different values of these parameters. Using the published Event Horizon Telescope measurements of M87\(^*\) and Sgr A\(^*\), we constrain the Yang-Mills charge and the power parameter from the angular size and the Schwarzschild deviation \(\delta\) of the observed images. At the Maxwell point \(q = 1\) the spin marginalized likelihood of M87\(^*\) bounds the charge to \(Q \lesssim 0.29\,M\) at \(1\sigma\), while the fixed-spin band intersection at \(a = 0.7\,M\) gives the weaker \(Q \lesssim 0.52\,M\) from the M87\(^*\) angular size alone. The bound weakens as \(q \to 3/2\), where the shadow diameter becomes nearly insensitive to the charge. The shadow radius also fixes the limiting absorption cross section at high frequencies and hence the energy emission rate, which is suppressed by the charge and enhanced by the power parameter. We then compute the quasinormal modes of a massless scalar on the rotating background from the leading-order Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin (WKB) conditions on the Teukolsky type radial potential, finding that the oscillation frequency rises and the damping rate falls as the charge or spin increases. The power parameter leaves an imprint on the shadow size and its charge sensitivity and in the quasinormal spectrum the shift is in principle present but lies below the resolution of current detectors.
papers.authors: I. Ezzaki, A. El Boukili, H. Lekbich, A. Benami

papers.title: Effects of Solar Wind Plasma Noise on Stochastic Gravitational Wave Background Searches with a Space Based Interferometer Network
papers.abstract: The LISA-Taiji dual detector network improves millihertz SGWB sensitivity through cross correlation measurements. Solar wind plasma, however, can generate plasma noise correlated between detectors and bias SGWB cross correlation estimates. We use high time resolution electron density data from Wind/SWE, estimate the solar wind electron density fluctuation spectrum with the Lomb-Scargle method, and propagate the resulting plasma noise to the TDI A/E channels of the LISA-Taiji network. By including finite arm propagation, Taylor frozen flow spatial correlations, and the network overlap reduction response, we compute the SGWB parameter bias induced by interdetector plasma noise. Although the single detector plasma residual is below the reference noise, the component correlated between detectors can enter the SGWB cross correlation estimator directly. Under dual detector scale coverage, the plasma induced parameter bias for a power law SGWB can reach $12.73\%$ of the corresponding Fisher parameter uncertainty. For M2/M3 cosmic string spectra, the bias in $\ln G\mu$ can reach $19.26\%$ of the corresponding Fisher parameter uncertainty for the network configurations, observing times, and frequency bands considered here. These results show that the impact of solar wind plasma noise cannot be assessed from the single detector residual noise level alone. In LISA-Taiji SGWB searches, the interdetector correlated component of this noise can directly affect parameter estimation.
papers.authors: Mengfei Sun, Borui Wang, Jie Wu, Jin Li, Shengyi Ye

papers.title: Controlling Waiting Time Statistics in Monitored Collective Spins: Mitigating Detector's Resolution Barrier in Measurement-Induced Phase Transitions
papers.abstract: In collective dissipative spin systems, the postselection barrier can be partially mitigated; however, a further obstacle may be posed by the finite temporal resolution of detectors. In this work, we investigate how initial-state inhomogeneities can control waiting-time statistics between quantum jumps, thereby mitigating the detector-resolution problem. We consider a collectively monitored spin model with a boundary time-crystalline phase, introducing inhomogeneity by partitioning the ensemble into two subsystems rotated by an angle $\theta$. We find that the measurement-induced phase transition survives under inhomogeneities, with different entanglement scaling regimes. The waiting time increases with $\theta$, scaling as $1/N$ but with a prefactor strongly enhanced by orders of magnitude, and in the anti-aligned limit $\theta = \pi$ it remains finite, fully resolving the resolution barrier. This mitigation, however, comes at a cost: the entanglement saturation time becomes significantly longer, partially reintroducing the postselection barrier. Our results highlight a trade-off between detector resolution and postselection overhead, with direct implications for the experimental observation of measurement-induced phenomena.
papers.authors: Tanbir Islam, Fernando Iemini

papers.title: Poisson bracket and $L_\infty$ algebras
papers.abstract: We describe the Poisson bracket of a Lagrangian field theory expressed in the framework of $L_\infty$ algebras. If the symplectic structure on phase space is defined following recent work, we show that the Poisson bracket can be computed with the Peierls formula, confirming the well-known result of the covariant phase space formalism. Of particular interest is the Poisson bracket in nonlocal theories. In $p$-adic string theory we find that a straightforward construction of the Poisson bracket is obstructed by higher derivative instabilities. We also discuss the inverse relation between the Poisson bracket and symplectic structure in the language of homological algebra, extending some ideas in the mathematical physics literature.
papers.authors: Vin\'icius Bernardes, Theodore Erler, Atakan Hilmi F{\i}rat, Igor Khavkine

papers.title: Cancellation of one-loop time dependence in superhorizon curvature perturbations from all scales
